_about: Universal layout-engine config. All thresholds, conventions, and weights live here. No circuit names or component-specific logic — edits to this file change behavior across every circuit class without code changes.

unified_chat._comment: One-AI mode (2026-06-18, user policy 'now only one ai'). When enabled the chat exposes ALL tools (schematic + PCB) and a unified system prompt regardless of which editor opened the panel, so a single assistant runs the whole flow (build/edit schematic -> ERC -> PCB place/route -> DRC -> Gerber) and edits an existing design OR creates one from scratch. Read by agent.py:_unified_chat_enabled. Set enabled=false to restore the legacy per-editor page-scoped behaviour (eeschema panel = schematic tools only, pcbnew panel = PCB tools only). 2026-06-21: user reverted to page-scoped. 2026-06-22: user RE-ENABLED -- wants ONE COMMON AI for the whole KiCad ('appadi illa common ai for whole kicad'), not sch-page=sch-prompt / pcb-page=pcb-prompt. This also removes the stale-PCB-scope-blocks-build problem since the prompt+tools no longer depend on the panel's reported page.
unified_chat._project_awareness_comment: Whole-project understanding (2026-06-30). When true, every chat turn is given a manifest of EVERY KiCad design file in the project folder (.kicad_pro/.kicad_sch/.kicad_pcb) with a one-line summary each (parts/wires for schematics, footprints/tracks for boards) and the active file marked. So the one common AI knows the whole project — the user can ask about or edit ANY file, not just the one open in front of them. project_awareness_max_files caps how many files get the deep one-line summary (the rest are listed by name+type) to keep big projects fast. false => no manifest, byte-identical to before. Read by agent.py:_build_project_manifest_block.

build_flow._comment: Cursor / coding-agent build flow (2026-06-22, user: 'first folder create pannitu tha circuit create panna permission kekkanum ... appadi thana cursor claude eppadi work aakuthu'). When folder_first=true (default), a NEW whole-circuit request runs: (1) ask Project name -> (2) call create_project to make the EMPTY project folder+files (loads in Project Files, ALWAYS succeeds) -> (3) ask the design questions -> (4) build_circuit with out_path=<the created .kicad_sch> to fill the circuit INTO that project. The workspace exists before its contents, so a circuit with doubts/errors never costs the user the folder. Read by agent.py:_folder_first_enabled, which appends FOLDER_FIRST_RULE and SUPPRESSES the one-step ASK_ASSUMPTIONS_RULE + PROJECT_NAMING_RULE (whose ordering would contradict it). Set false to restore the legacy one-step flow (ask design questions, then build folder+circuit together in one build_circuit call).
build_flow._confirm_each_step_doc: Cursor-style step approval (2026-06-25, user: 'erc clean next step update pcb polama kekkanum ... user permission kudutha aprom tha nee aatha pannnum ... aprom tha user ku puriyum ai enna pannuthunu'). When true, the AI runs the build pipeline as APPROVED STEPS instead of one black box: it tells the user what it will do and asks before each major action — ERC check, ERC fix, PCB update, layout, score. Concretely build_circuit STOPS after the schematic (ERC-cleaned) and DEFERS the PCB (summary.pcb.deferred); the agent then asks 'ERC clean — update the PCB now?' and only on OK calls generate_pcb. Read by build_circuit (defer PCB) + agent.py (appends STEP_CONFIRMATION_RULE). Set false for the legacy one-shot build (schematic + PCB + finish in one call).

project_naming._comment: Cursor-style project naming (2026-06-21, user request: 'cursor folder structure ku user-kitta kekkuma, athu maathiri kicad-layum venum'). When enabled the agent proposes a project name + folder path INSIDE the NEW-circuit build preview (a 'Project:' and 'Folder:' line just above 'Want me to build it?'), and the user can override the name/folder before confirming -- exactly like Cursor showing the file tree before it writes. The agreed name flows build_circuit(project_name=...) -> RouterState.project_name -> graphs/nodes/render.py, which sets ir.name so the per-circuit folder, the .kicad_sch basename, the child sheet files and the title block all follow the user's chosen name instead of the architect's auto ir.name. Read by agent.py:_project_naming_enabled (appends PROJECT_NAMING_RULE to the system prompt) and render_node (the ir.name override, only when project_name is set AND out_path is empty). Set enabled=false (propose_in_preview=false) to restore the fully-automatic naming -- byte-stable: the prompt prefix drops the suffix and, with no project_name in state, render_node is unchanged. Ignored when overwriting an open file (out_path set keeps that file's name).

sheet_decision._comment: Phase 14. Auto-decision: single sheet vs single+blocks vs multi-sheet hierarchy. Three regimes: SMALL = no blocks (just flat); MEDIUM = single sheet with block rectangles; LARGE = hierarchical multi-sheet (parent + child .kicad_sch files). Tune per project here — no hardcoded thresholds in engine.py.
sheet_decision._post_architect_relayout_comment: User policy (2026-06-05): the pre-architect 'Choose layout' node guesses the 3-way mode (FLAT / SINGLE_SHEET_BLOCKS / HIERARCHY) from PROMPT KEYWORDS only, which is unstable -- the same 'design a complete CAN logger' prompt scored complexity 69 -> HIERARCHY on one run and 54 -> FLAT on the next, flipping the layout for an identical board. When true (default), render_node re-decides the 3-way from the ACTUAL block count the architect emitted (SINGLE_SHEET_BLOCKS if blocks>=hierarchy_min_blocks, HIERARCHY if blocks>single_sheet_max_blocks), so the layout follows the real board, not the prompt phrasing. Only overrides an AUTO decision -- an explicit user 'single sheet' / 'hierarchy' request is left untouched. Set false to trust the pre-architect prompt-keyword guess.
sheet_decision._single_sheet_max_blocks_comment: User policy (2026-06-03, set back to 5): single-sheet-with-blocks holds up to this many functional blocks; ABOVE it render() forces multi-sheet hierarchy (A2 is NOT allowed). 6+ functional groups (e.g. the STM32+CAN+microSD data logger: POWER_INPUT/5V_REG/3V3_REG/MCU/CAN/SD/PROTECTION/INDICATORS...) go multi-sheet. Driven by the ACTUAL block count the architect emitted, not the pre-architect prompt-keyword estimate.
sheet_decision._size_override_beats_single_sheet_commen: User policy (2026-06-03): part COUNT is the second physical limit on one A3 sheet. When true, a force_single_sheet design (auto- OR user-requested 'make it single sheet') that stays UNDER single_sheet_max_blocks but emits > large_min_components in >= 2 blocks is rendered multi-sheet hierarchy instead — same as the n_blk > single_sheet_max_blocks term, but on component count. Catches dense boards that fit the block cap yet overflow the sheet (STM32 + CAN + microSD data logger ~60 parts in 7-9 blocks). Set false to restore legacy behaviour where force_single_sheet always wins below the block cap.
sheet_decision._escalate_on_geometric_overflow_comment: HARD RULE ([[feedback_layout_within_sheet]]) — the authoritative, geometry-based backstop to the COUNT proxies above. After render_flat lays out a single-sheet-with-blocks board AND grows the page to the size cap (A3; A2/A1 banned, L12), it measures the REAL content bbox; if it still exceeds the usable area (page minus margins minus title-block reserve) on either axis, the board is split into a multi-sheet hierarchy instead of being top/left-aligned with the surplus spilling off the bottom-right border (the 'circuit outside the sheet' defect). Block/part COUNT only approximates 'fits one sheet'; a 64-pin STM32 + full decoupling + dual crystals passes both count gates (~30 parts, 5 blocks) yet overflows A3. Fires only when the layout genuinely does not fit, so boards that DO fit are byte-identical (non-breaking). Set false to restore the legacy count-only decision (an over-large flat board then renders off-sheet).
sheet_decision._geometric_overflow_tol_mm_comment: Slack (mm, ~1 grid step) before the geometric-overflow split fires, so a layout that fits within a hair of the usable area is not split needlessly.
sheet_decision._rule: use_hierarchy = force_hierarchy OR (n_blk > single_sheet_max_blocks) OR (n_comp > large_min AND n_blk >= 2) OR (n_blk >= hierarchy_min_blocks AND n_comp > small_max). BOTH the (n_blk > single_sheet_max_blocks) term AND the (n_comp > large_min AND n_blk >= 2) term override a force_single_sheet flag (the latter gated by size_override_beats_single_sheet). force_hierarchy comes from build_circuit's flag (user explicitly asks 'as multi-sheet').

recenter_content._comment: Page-aware re-centring. The placer anchors everything at the fixed module constant SHEET_CENTRE (148.59, 105.41) = A4 centre. When the dynamic paper picker chooses A3+ for a multi-block single sheet, content built around the A4 centre clusters in the TOP-LEFT corner of the bigger sheet (the 'oorama' / corner bug). After placement, this pass measures the content bounding box and translates EVERY component so the bbox centre lands on the real paper centre. Purely additive: positions only; wires/labels/junctions are derived downstream from component positions so they follow automatically. Disable (enabled=false) for byte-identical legacy output.
recenter_content._clear_title_block_note: When true, the vertical target is the centre of the band ABOVE the bottom-right title block (page_h - title_block_h)/2 instead of the geometric page centre, biasing content up so large designs never overlap the title block. Default false keeps A4 single-IC output centred on the true page centre (delta ~0 -> unchanged).
recenter_content._min_shift_note: Skip the shift entirely when both |dx| and |dy| are below this — keeps already-centred renders (A4 single-IC) byte-identical.

keep_inside_sheet._comment: HARD RULE ([[feedback_layout_within_sheet]]): the finished design must stay INSIDE the printable sheet border and clear of the bottom-right title block. Runs dead-last in render_flat + child-sheet render, AFTER every placement + relocation pass (decoupling/crystal hug, connector-edge snap, block reflow + title-block lift) — those passes move individual parts to satisfy local rules and can push the content bbox past the page edge the initial grid centring kept it inside (the 'components cross the red border' defect). This pass measures the FINAL content bbox and, when it crosses a border, rigidly TRANSLATES the whole design (positions only; wires/labels/junctions derive from pin positions downstream so they follow) the minimum on-grid distance to bring it back in-bounds. CLAMP, not centre: a design already inside the border is left byte-identical (the common A4 single-IC case is a no-op), so it is safe to leave on. Set enabled=false for legacy byte-identical output. A margin_mm edge omitted falls back to placement.page_margin_mm; the 12.7 mm (500 mil) default is looser than the placer's 18 mm so the net only fires on a real crossing.
keep_inside_sheet._clear_title_block_note: When true, the bottom usable edge is pulled up to the title-block top (page_h - title_block_h) so content is clamped clear of the bottom-right title block. When false, only the page margins bound the clamp.
keep_inside_sheet._include_field_text_note: When true (default), the clamp measures each part's field-text-aware bbox (_abs_bbox_with_fields) instead of the body-only outer bbox, so a part whose BODY is in-bounds but whose RefDes/Value text spills across the border or onto the title block is still pulled back. Set false for byte-identical body-only legacy measurement.
keep_inside_sheet._grow_page_if_overflow_note: When true (default), if the FINISHED content is larger than the chosen page's usable area, the page is grown to the next size in hierarchy_layout.page_size_priority that fits (A4->A3) BEFORE the clamp top/left-aligns it — measured on real post-placement geometry. Bounded by the priority list (never A2/A1 per L12). Set false to keep the legacy behaviour where an over-large flat sheet is shoved off the bottom-right edge instead of growing.

decoupling_auto_add._comment: Phase 12. add_decoupling verb auto-adds HF + bulk caps on every VDD-like pin of a target IC. All values + pin patterns config-driven so per-project tuning needs ZERO code changes.

erc_check._comment: Phase 19a. kicad-cli wrapper for ERC. Severity-all so we surface warnings too. Disable by setting enabled=false if kicad-cli isn't on PATH.
erc_check._run_on_copy_note: Fix (2026-06-08) for the ERC-timeout-while-open bug. When KiCad has the project open it holds a `~<name>.kicad_sch.lck`, and kicad-cli HANGS reading the locked file (measured: locked original times out at 30s vs an unlocked COPY finishing in 10s — a LOCK, not slowness, so a bigger timeout won't help). When true, erc_check copies the whole project (all .kicad_sch + .kicad_pro + any local *-lib-table) into a throwaway temp dir and runs ERC there, then persists the report next to the original — so ERC + the erc_autofix regression guard work WHILE the file is open in KiCad. Set false to run directly on the original (legacy; times out on a locked file).

export_docs._comment: Phase 21. One-call doc pack: schematic PDF + SVG + PCB 3D PNGs + BOM CSV + README.md. All written into <sch_dir>/docs/. Universal. Toggle stages via `include_*` flags or per-call args.

ship_design._comment: Phase 18e. One-prompt finisher — runs ERC, BOM, DRC, Gerbers, 3D render in sequence and returns a single report. Disable any stage by setting `enabled: false` inside its `steps` entry. Set `strict: true` on DRC to fail the report on any DRC error (default is lenient because empty/un-routed boards report 'no Edge.Cuts' which is expected).
ship_design._block_export_comment: Hard fab-export gate. When true, real DRC errors (>0) BLOCK the Gerber/drill/ZIP stage entirely instead of exporting and merely marking the report NOT READY — a board with open DRC errors never reaches a manufacturer. Default false preserves the legacy export-anyway behaviour.

render_pcb_3d._comment: Phase 18d. kicad-cli pcb render -> PNG 3D views. Default top+bottom @1600x900 'basic' quality (fast, ~2-3 sec each). Use 'high' for marketing screenshots (~30 sec). Universal.

drc_check._comment: Phase 19c. kicad-cli wrapper for PCB Design Rules Check. Universal — works for any .kicad_pcb. Pairs with erc_check (schematic-side). Reports clearance violations, unrouted nets, hole-to-edge clearance, etc. Set schematic_parity=true to also verify the PCB matches the schematic netlist.
drc_check._timeout_scaling_comment: P3.1 (2026-05-26). Actual DRC timeout = max(timeout_seconds, timeout_seconds + footprint_count * timeout_per_footprint_ms / 1000), capped at timeout_max_seconds. kicad-cli's DRC scales roughly linearly with footprint + track count; the original fixed 60 s killed runs on anything over ~100 footprints. Set timeout_per_footprint_ms=0 to restore the fixed-budget behaviour.

route_pcb_simple._comment: Phase 25 v1. Best-effort L-shaped Manhattan router for SHORT nets — connects 2-to-N-pad nets on a single layer (F.Cu by default) using a minimum spanning tree of L-shaped traces. NOT a replacement for a real autorouter (FreeRouting) — it does no via insertion, no multi-layer routing, no length matching, no diff-pair handling. Intended for the easy cases: decoupling caps to IC pins, short pull-ups, simple connector fanout. Long / complex nets are SKIPPED and reported in the result so the user knows to route them manually or via a real autorouter. GND-like nets default to SKIP because they're served by the auto_zones_pcb copper pour.
route_pcb_simple._max_pads_comment: Skip nets with more pads than this. A 12-pad MCU power net is best left to a real router (or the GND pour).
route_pcb_simple._max_net_span_comment: Skip a net when the bounding box of its pads exceeds this on either axis. Stops the simple router from drawing kilometre-long zig-zags across the whole board. Set to 0 (default) for AUTO — scaled to the board's actual pad-bbox diagonal via max_net_span_diag_factor. The old 60 mm fixed cap silently dropped legitimate power rails on any board > 80 mm wide.
route_pcb_simple._max_net_span_diag_factor_comment: P2.1 (2026-05-26). Multiplier on the pad-bbox diagonal when max_net_span_mm=0. 1.0 = full diagonal (allow any rail that fits on the board). Lower to skip nets spanning more than X% of the board.
route_pcb_simple._track_width_comment: Used when the net's class doesn't define one and no override is passed. Net-class width (from set_design_rules) is preferred when available.
route_pcb_simple._skip_nets_comment: Net names that should NEVER be routed as discrete traces. Ground nets are handled by auto_zones_pcb's copper pour; the unconnected '' entry stops us from routing the implicit no-net pad.
route_pcb_simple._obstacle_inflate_comment: Pad bbox of OTHER footprints is inflated by this much when checking whether an L-shape crosses a body. Bigger = safer but skips more routes.
route_pcb_simple._clearance_aware_comment: Root-cause fix (2026-06-25) for the simple router creating SHORTS. When true, every candidate track is rejected unless it stays (own_half_width + clearance + obstacle_half_width) away from EVERY other net — both other nets' pads AND their already-routed tracks (tracked per layer this run). Clearance is the board's real Default-netclass clearance from the .kicad_pro (dynamic, no hardcode); falls back to default_clearance_mm. A net that can't be routed within clearance is left as ratsnest, NEVER shorted. Set false for the legacy short-prone behaviour.
route_pcb_simple._edge_clearance_comment: R2.2. Keep routed tracks at least this far from the Edge.Cuts outline (read from the ACTUAL board shape, any board) so the router never makes a copper_edge_clearance DRC error. Dynamic, no fixed geometry. false/0 disables.
route_pcb_simple._respect_existing_copper_comment: Root-cause fix (2026-06-26) for compose-shorts. route_pcb_simple is called repeatedly in the pipeline (route + ensure_ground_return + repair + ripup); each call previously started with an EMPTY obstacle set and was blind to the copper the earlier calls laid, so it routed over it -> shorting_items / tracks_crossing. true (default) seeds every existing segment + via on the board as an obstacle so each pass keeps clear of all prior copper (other nets); same-net copper is still free to extend. A fresh F8 board has no tracks, so first-pass routing is byte-stable. Set false only to restore the old single-pass-only behaviour.
route_pcb_simple._skip_pad_overlap_comment: When the L-segment passes within this distance of the segment endpoints' OWN pad bbox we keep it (it should overlap the pads it connects to). Otherwise we'd reject every valid route.
route_pcb_simple._preview_only_comment: When true, return the route list WITHOUT mutating the .kicad_pcb. Useful as a dry-run before committing tracks.
route_pcb_simple._replace_existing_comment: When true, delete every existing track segment on `layer` before routing. Off by default — the user may have manual tracks they want kept.
route_pcb_simple._enable_z_detour_comment: v2 (2026-05-26): when both L-shape candidates fail (other-net pads in the way), try Z-shape (3-segment) detours that bend AROUND obstacles. Searches outward from the y-midpoint in `z_step_mm` increments up to `z_max_offset_mm`. Closes many simple-block routes that v1 was skipping.
route_pcb_simple._enable_vias_comment: v2: when L AND Z fail, drop a via at the L-corner and finish the route on the back layer. Cap per net via `max_vias_per_net`. Useful for boards where the front layer has too many obstacles for a flat route.
route_pcb_simple._max_vias_per_net_comment: Hard cap on via insertions per net so one dense net can't fill the board with stitching. 4 is enough for short signal nets; bump for power distribution if needed.
route_pcb_simple._max_vias_per_class_comment: R1.3 (2026-05-26). Per-net-class via budget override. Power and GND nets often need 8-16 stitching vias to bridge zone returns and are starved by the global max_vias_per_net=4. Net class is looked up from .kicad_pro's netclass_patterns; any class not listed here uses max_vias_per_net.
route_pcb_simple._layer_axis_policy_comment: R1.2 (2026-05-26). Per-layer preferred routing axis. F.Cu defaults to 'h' (horizontal-first L-shape) and B.Cu to 'v' (vertical-first) — standard two-layer PCB convention. When both L candidates clear the obstacle list, the policy-preferred one wins. Set 'any' to keep the legacy [h, v] order. Universal — works for any board; project can override per layer (e.g. 4-layer with In1.Cu signals horizontal, In2.Cu power, etc.).
route_pcb_simple._enable_astar_comment: R1.1 (2026-05-26). When L + Z + via all fail, fall through to A* Manhattan-grid search. Pure-Python heapq; only the residual ~5% of edges reach this tier so cost is bounded. Set false to disable and skip those edges instead.

voltage_clearance._comment: R1 (IPC-2221B). When true, the board routing clearance is scaled up to the IPC requirement for the HIGHEST voltage present (voltage parsed from net names: +12V, 3V3, 230V). Conservative board-level bump — always safe, never under-spaced; low-voltage-only boards are unaffected (their max voltage maps to the base clearance). ipc_table is ascending [[max_voltage, clearance_mm]] for external uncoated conductors. false (default) = clearance unchanged = byte-stable.

domain_clearance._comment: R12 routing-side isolation. When true, a SENSITIVE net (name matches pcb_constraint_model.json pin_signatures.analog: ADC/SENSE/CELL/VREF...) and a NOISY net (matches power_switch sigs or net_signatures.motor_power: SW/GATE/MOTOR...) each route with extra copper clearance to everything, so analog traces keep their distance from switching/motor traces. Reuses the reasoning signatures (no duplicate net list). false (default) = byte-stable.

route_pcb_simple._route_priority_order_comment: Phase 3 of the Universal PCB engine (R11). When true, nets are routed critical (high-speed/clock) -> power -> signal instead of net-id order, so critical nets claim clean channels before the board congests. Priority is derived from the SAME pcb_constraint_model.json pin_signatures (highspeed/clock/power) — one source of truth, no duplicate net-name list. The router stays clearance-aware, so reordering only changes which net wins a corridor, never makes a short. Enabled 2026-06-30 (was false/net-id order); set false to restore byte-stable net-id order.
route_pcb_simple._astar_step_mm_comment: Grid pitch for A*. 1.27 mm = 50 mil, matches the schematic-side KiCad grid. Smaller = finer routing but exponentially more nodes; larger = coarser but faster.
route_pcb_simple._astar_bounds_margin_mm_comment: Search bbox is the rect (a + b) inflated by this margin on each side. Bounds the search so A* never wanders the entire board for a short edge. Bump if obstacles force long detours.
route_pcb_simple._astar_max_nodes_comment: Hard cap on nodes explored per call. Hitting the cap returns None and the caller skips the edge — prevents A* from spinning on truly unroutable edges. 50k handles ~150 mm × 150 mm boards at 1.27 mm grid.
route_pcb_simple._corner_chamfer_mm_comment: R2.3 (2026-05-27). 45° bevel length on right-angle corners — per rule 'Avoid 90-degree bends; use 45-degree bends'. Each 90° L-corner gets replaced with two perpendicular segments meeting via a chamfer_mm-long diagonal. Rejected per corner when the diagonal would clip an obstacle (kept square). Set 0 to disable; bump to 1.0 for more visible bevels on wider boards.

pcb_verify._comment: Phase 27. Composite 'after-every-PCB-mutation' verifier. Runs drc_check + render_pcb_3d in sequence and returns ONE compact card the chat can render inline. Mirrors the schematic-side render-then-ERC workflow ([[feedback_render_erc_chat_workflow]]). The agent is taught (system prompt) to call pcb_verify automatically after any PCB-mutating tool so the user always sees the post-change state without typing.

drc._strict_comment: When true, ANY DRC error fails the verify; when false (default) we report the count but still mark verify as 'ok' if the board is just unrouted. Mirrors ship_design.steps.drc.strict.

render._comment: Optional: skip the 3D render if the user is iterating quickly and the render delay (~3s) feels chatty. The DRC line still ships either way.

silkscreen._comment: R2.4 (2026-05-27). Pre-fab check: flags silkscreen items (fp_text / fp_line / fp_poly) that overlap pads of the same footprint — per rule 'Avoid silkscreen on pads'. Bboxes are inflated by `pad_inflate_mm` so silk that grazes the pad edge is still flagged.

card_template._comment: Wording for the per-stage line of the verify card. {n} = error count, {w} = warning count, {img_top} / {img_bottom} = render file basenames.

pcb_quality._comment: Scored 'perfect PCB' analyzer (tool: pcb_quality). READ-ONLY — walks a .kicad_pcb and emits one card: Placement / Routing / Power / Signal-Layers / Manufacturing %, an overall score + verdict, and Apply-Fix suggestions that each name an EXISTING mutating tool. Every threshold below is verified against authoritative sources (cited inline), not invented. Disable the whole tool with enabled=false.
pcb_quality._show_percentage_comment: User prefers plain words over a number (2026-06-25: 'ennaku percentage vendam'). When false, each dimension + the overall show the verdict WORD (EXCELLENT/GOOD/REVIEW/NEEDS WORK) instead of a %, and the agent is told not to quote a score. Set true to restore numeric scoring.
pcb_quality._ic_ref_prefixes_comment: Refdes prefixes treated as ICs (the parts decoupling caps must sit next to). U = standard IC prefix.
pcb_quality._ic_min_pads_comment: A footprint with >= this many pads is also treated as an IC even if its refdes isn't in ic_ref_prefixes (catches modules/connectors acting as the main part). 6 excludes 2-pad passives and 3-pad regulators/transistors.
pcb_quality._decap_value_patterns_comment: What counts as a decoupling cap = its Value matches one of these regexes (case-insensitive, matched at start). Default = the universal 100nF / 0.1uF bypass in its common spellings (100n, 0.1u, 0.1µ, 0u1, n100). DATA not CIRCUIT: edit to treat other values as decaps (e.g. add '^\s*1\s*u' to include 1uF) — nothing about a specific board is baked into code.
pcb_quality._decap_max_mm_comment: HEURISTIC PROXY (warn, not error). A 100nF decoupling cap further than this from its nearest IC is flagged. VERIFIED: what actually matters is mounting INDUCTANCE (~1 nH per mm of loop), not raw distance — ideal placement is 1-2 mm, < 3 mm for >100 MHz parts (Sierra Circuits / Cadence). 5 mm is the loose outer bound that catches gross misplacement (the '18 mm away' case) without false-flagging tight-but-not-perfect layouts. Lower to 3.0 for high-speed-strict boards. Sources: protoexpress.com/blog/decoupling-capacitor-placement-guidelines-pcb-design, resources.pcb.cadence.com/blog/2020-decoupling-capacitor-placement-in-pcb-layout
pcb_quality._min_board_efficiency_comment: ADVISORY ONLY (never scored). If (sum of footprint pad-bbox area / board-outline area) is below this, surface a 'consider shrink-to-fit' suggestion. Set LOW (0.05) on purpose: pad-bbox area badly under-counts the true area a board needs (routing channels, connectors, keepout, mounting holes are all empty of pads), so a higher threshold would false-flag normal boards. No IPC standard for board density — this only catches the egregiously empty outline (e.g. 3 parts on a 100x80 board).
pcb_quality._stack_min_mm_comment: Placement score: two footprints whose CENTRES are within this distance (mm) count as 'stacked' — the real auto-place failure mode (parts on top of each other / all at 0,0). Centre-based on purpose so a decap placed 1 mm off an IC (ideal practice) is NOT flagged. True courtyard-overlap-at-a-distance is left to kicad-cli DRC, which does it precisely.
pcb_quality._gnd_net_regex_comment: Identifies ground nets for the copper-pour / plane check. Matches the GND token anywhere (GND/AGND/DGND/PGND/GNDA) plus VSS (IC ground pin) and EARTH. Deliberately NOT '^G?N?D' which would wrongly match nets like DATA.

weights._comment: Overall score = weighted average of the dimensions that actually ran (renormalised — a dimension that is n/a, e.g. no power nets, is dropped, not zeroed). Power weighted highest because an under-sized power trace is a burn/brownout risk; manufacturing/DRC next because it gates fab. Must sum is NOT required (renormalised).

pcb_quality._bands_comment: Overall-score -> verdict label. First band whose threshold the score meets wins (descending).

steps._drc_comment: Fold REAL kicad-cli DRC into the Manufacturing dimension. Set false (or pass skip_drc:true) for a fast static-only score when iterating.

pcb_quality._reference_rules_comment: Documented-but-not-yet-auto-checked rules from the layer/routing spec, captured here so route_pcb_simple / a future layer-aware check can consume verified values instead of re-researching. NONE of these are enforced by the scorer yet.

reference_rules._stackup_comment: SGPS is the standard 4-layer stackup: GND on L2 directly under top-signal gives a low-impedance return path + EMI control; power on L3 couples to L2 for plane capacitance. Source: resources.pcb.cadence.com/blog/best-formats-for-4-layer-pcb-stackups
reference_rules._orthogonal_comment: 2-layer strict rule: adjacent layers route orthogonally (one H, one V, change direction via a via) -> fewer crossings + less inter-layer crosstalk. Source: resources.pcb.cadence.com/blog/simple-strategies-for-double-sided-2-layer-pcbs
reference_rules._routing_priority_comment: Route order: power/ground + critical clocks & diff-pairs FIRST (stable reference, shortest critical nets), then other high-speed, then sensitive analog, then general GPIO. Source: protoexpress.com/blog/best-high-speed-pcb-routing-practices
reference_rules._via_current_comment: IPC-2152, 20 µm plating, 10 °C rise: a 0.3 mm drill via carries ~0.8-1.0 A; use bigger/multiple vias for power (10 A ~= 10-13x 0.3 mm vias). Source: queenems.com/blog/pcb-via-current-capacity

pcb_improve._comment: Score-driven, GUARDED auto-fix loop (tool: pcb_improve) — the 'Apply Fix' half of the perfect-PCB loop. Scores via pcb_quality, applies the fixes it recommends, re-scores, repeats. Every fix is kept ONLY if the overall score did not drop (board snapshotted + restored on regression), so the percentage is monotonic. Fully dynamic: the fix list is whatever pcb_quality emits for THIS board — no step sequence hardcoded. Contrast auto_layout_pcb, which runs a fixed full pipeline blindly with no score guard.
pcb_improve._target_score_comment: Stop once the overall pcb_quality score reaches this %. 90 = the 'EXCELLENT' band. Raise toward 100 to push harder (more passes), lower for a quick lift.
pcb_improve._max_passes_comment: Hard cap on full score→fix→rescore rounds. Each pass tries every recommended fix tool once. 3 is plenty for the current fix set; the loop also exits early when a pass makes no improvement.
pcb_improve._min_gain_comment: A fix is KEPT only if it raises the overall score by at least this many points; otherwise the board is reverted to its pre-fix bytes. >0 so a no-op or marginal fix can't churn the file. This is the no-regression guard.
pcb_improve._loop_skip_drc_comment: Use the fast static score (no kicad-cli DRC) DURING the loop so iterating is quick; the FINAL reported score always runs real DRC. Set false to score with DRC every iteration (slower, stricter guard).
pcb_improve._fix_tools_comment: Allowlist of mutating tools the loop may invoke. A pcb_quality finding names one of these as its fix; only listed tools run. Remove one to forbid the loop from using it (e.g. drop auto_place_pcb to keep manual placement).
pcb_improve._fix_tool_args_comment: Per-tool extra args merged with {pcb_path}. drc_autofix needs apply:true to actually write fixes. Other tools run with their own config defaults.

auto_mounting_holes_pcb._comment: Phase 26a. Drop N NPTH mounting holes on a .kicad_pcb, inset from the corners of the Edge.Cuts outline. Universal — works on any board once auto_outline_pcb has produced an outline. Pure data: change the hole size by editing diameter_mm; M3 default (3.2 mm clearance for an M3 screw with washer). `inset_mm` is the corner-to-hole-center distance. `corner_strategy=4` places one hole at each of the 4 corners (standard); set to 2 to place only diagonally opposite holes for small boards.
auto_mounting_holes_pcb._replace_existing_comment: When true, remove any pre-existing mounting-hole footprints (lib_id matching `library_id`) before placing new ones. Off if user manually positioned mounting holes and wants them kept.

auto_fiducials_pcb._comment: Phase 26b. Place fiducial markers on a .kicad_pcb so pick-and-place machines can register the board. Default: 3 fiducials at bottom-left, top-left, top-right corners (asymmetric pattern lets the P&P decide board orientation). 2-fiducial mode for small boards: just bottom-left + top-right. Pad geometry follows the standard 1 mm copper / 2 mm mask opening per IPC-7351.
auto_fiducials_pcb._clearance_comment: min_clearance_mm = keep each fiducial this far from existing pads (mounting holes). pour_clearance_extra_mm = extra gap added to the fiducial's mask radius so the GND pour stays outside its mask opening (kills solder_mask_bridge). The fiducial's clearance is COMPUTED from its own mask/pad size — works for any fiducial, nothing hardcoded.
auto_fiducials_pcb._strategy_comment: 3-fiducial layout: BL + TL + TR (skip BR — asymmetric so P&P can detect orientation). 2-fiducial layout: BL + TR (diagonal). Set count=2 or 3.

ripup_reroute._comment: Pure-Python rip-up-and-reroute (tools/ripup_reroute_pcb.py). For each still-unconnected net, rips up the tracks blocking it (other nets' segments inside its pad bbox + ripup_margin_mm), routes it, and re-routes the ripped nets — committing ONLY if kicad-cli DRC then shows fewer unconnected pads, else reverting the board file byte-for-byte. NEVER makes the board worse. No Java/GPU/external router. enabled=false (default) = no-op. Best run after route_pcb_simple + ensure_ground_return; helps track-congested (SMD) boards, not THT pad-congestion.

ensure_ground_return._comment: Phase 3 of the Universal PCB engine (Fix 1, R5). Runs AFTER auto_zones_pcb in the auto_layout step list. Proves every skipped ground net (route_pcb_simple.skip_nets) is served by a FILLED copper zone; for any that is not (pour absent / empty), routes that net on route_layer so ground is never silently orphaned (the NE555 bug: GND skipped by the router AND not poured). No-op when the pour covers ground. The ground-net set is route_pcb_simple.skip_nets (no duplicate list). enabled=false (DEFAULT, SAFE 2026-06-26): on a congested all-THT board the B.Cu GND star can cross signal tracks under the loaded clearance — keep off until isolated; enable per-board on SMD/roomier boards.

auto_thermal_vias_pcb._comment: Phase 26c. Add a stitched-via array under exposed-pad (thermal paddle) pads to dump heat from power ICs into internal/back-side copper. Universal: scans every footprint for a pad whose number matches `paddle_pad_numbers`; for each match, drops a configurable via grid centered on the pad. Use after F8 + auto_place_pcb so the paddle pad position is correct.
auto_thermal_vias_pcb._paddle_comment: Pad-number conventions vary: QFN often uses 'EP' or the highest pin number; SOT-223 + DPAK use '2'; ATmega/STM32 QFN sometimes 'PAD'. The default list covers the common conventions — add new ones here when a fab silently skips the paddle.
auto_thermal_vias_pcb._min_pad_comment: Skip vias under pads smaller than this — a 1 mm pad doesn't need thermal stitching and crowding small SMD pads with vias causes solder wicking.
auto_thermal_vias_pcb._ref_filter_comment: Empty = process every footprint. Set to a regex (e.g. 'U[0-9]+' or '^U[12]$') to limit thermal vias to specific refs.
auto_thermal_vias_pcb._replace_existing_comment: When true, delete previously-emitted thermal vias (vias inside any paddle pad bbox) before adding the new grid — idempotent re-run.

auto_zones_pcb._comment: Phase 18g. Adds GND copper pour zones on F.Cu + B.Cu. Eliminates ~90% of manual GND track routing. The zone polygon comes from Edge.Cuts (preferred) or the footprint bounding box (fallback). `replace_existing=true` clears prior zones on the same net so re-running the tool doesn't stack pours.

auto_outline_pcb._comment: Phase 18f. Draws a rectangular Edge.Cuts outline around the placed footprints. Fixes KiCad's `invalid_outline` DRC error which every fresh post-F8 board has. `replace_existing=true` clears any existing Edge.Cuts items first so re-running this tool doesn't stack outlines on top of each other.
auto_outline_pcb._copper_to_edge_min_mm_comment: R2.2 (2026-05-27). IPC-2221 minimum copper-to-edge distance. Most fabs (JLCPCB, PCBWay, OSHPark) reject boards below this. The actual outline margin is forced up to (fp_radius + copper_to_edge_min_mm) so even a project that sets margin_mm=0 still respects the fab minimum. Bump to 0.5 mm for tight V-cut panels.

auto_place_pcb._comment: Phase 18c. After Update PCB from Schematic (F8), components land stacked at origin (0,0). This tool arranges them in a grid grouped by refdes prefix. Universal — works for any board. Tune cell pitch + group ordering here without touching Python.
auto_place_pcb._group_order_note: Refdes-prefix priority left-to-right on the board. Unknown prefixes go to the end. Edit to change layout order.

ic_anchor._comment: P1.2 (2026-05-26). When no envil-blocks sidecar exists and the PCB has a clear IC (a single footprint with >= min_anchor_pads pads), place the IC at the board centre and fan satellites outward along the pin they share a net with. Decoupling caps on power nets land within decoupling_radius_mm; other passives at cluster_radius_mm. Connectors snap to sheet edges via the same regex set as connector_edge_placement. Falls back to the legacy refdes-grouped grid when the heuristic can't find a unique anchor (multiple equal candidates) or the board is too big (> max_components). Mirror of the schematic-side _place_components anchor-first path so the PCB layout matches the .kicad_sch.

refine._comment: P24 (2026-06-23). Placement-quality post-pass run by layout/place_refine.py after the chosen placement mode. (1) De-collision: each footprint's bbox (its *.CrtYd courtyard when present, else pad extents + pad_bbox_margin_mm) is pushed apart from every overlapping neighbour until they clear clearance_mm. (2) Wirelength refine: a few conservative force-directed sweeps nudge each movable part toward the centroid of the pads it connects to, accepting a move ONLY when it strictly shortens that part's net half-perimeter wirelength and adds no new overlap. Parts whose refdes prefix is in fixed_ref_prefixes (mounting holes, fiducials) never move. Set enabled=false for byte-stable pre-refine placement.
refine._rotation_comment: Gap-1 rotation optimizer (place_refine.py Phase 1.5). After de-collision, each movable part is tried at the listed orthogonal re-orientations (relative to its current angle) and kept at the one that strictly shortens the half-perimeter wirelength of the nets it touches without creating a new courtyard overlap. Cost-driven only — no per-part rules — so it generalises to any board. Connectors/mechanical parts (rot_skip_ref_prefixes) keep their keyed orientation. Set rotation_optimize=false for byte-stable no-rotation placement.
refine._railfilter_comment: High-fanout net suppression. GND/VCC rails touch many pads so their centroid sits at the board centre; pulling parts toward it cancels the signal-driven attraction and leaves parts scattered. Every attraction/cost pass (cluster, rotation, wirelength) ignores nets whose fanout exceeds max(wl_rail_min_degree, ceil(wl_rail_fraction * num_parts)) — purely topological (degree, not net names), so it scales: ~GND only on a 15-part board, true power rails on a 100-part board. Verified on ne555_blinker: signal HPWL 126.8->114.6 (-10%), overlaps 0. wl_rail_fraction=0 disables (byte-stable).
refine._cluster_comment: Bold force-directed clustering pre-pass (Phase 0): pulls each part most of the way to its signal-net centroid before de-collision. Helps scatter-grid LARGE boards but DEGRADES small dense boards (measured: ne555 signal HPWL 121.7->139.2 worse) because parts collapse then de-collision explodes them. Left OFF by default; enable per-board only when starting from a poor scattered placement.
refine._orientation_uniformity_comment: P5 (assembly DFM). When enabled, same-CLASS parts (grouped by refdes prefix — R, C, ... — not by component name) are snapped to their group's MAJORITY orthogonal orientation, but only when the snap creates no new courtyard overlap. Runs after the wirelength rotation optimizer (which can leave a group mixed). min_group = the smallest group worth unifying. Connectors/mechanical keep their keyed angle. enabled=false (default) -> orientation untouched -> byte-stable.
refine._constraint_placement_comment: Phase 2 of the Universal PCB engine (PCB_AI_ARCHITECTURE.md). When enabled, auto_place_pcb runs tools/pcb_reasoning to derive per-part electrical constraints and place_refine consumes them: keep-close pulls each support part (decoupling/clock/filter) toward the higher-criticality part it shares a net with, within its max_dist_mm; keep-away pushes domain-conflicting parts (analog away from switching, RF keepout) apart by min_gap_mm. Conservative: a move is reverted if it creates a courtyard overlap. enabled=false (default) -> place_refine gets constraints=None and output is byte-stable with Phase-1 behaviour. Flip enabled=true to activate reasoning-driven placement.

bom_export._comment: Phase 18b. kicad-cli wrapper for BOM CSV. NAMED PRESETS — pick via the `preset` arg on the export_bom tool call. Add new presets here without touching Python. Each preset specifies fields (the KiCad property names, including ${QUANTITY} / ${ITEM_NUMBER} / ${DNP} / ${EXCLUDE_FROM_BOM} / ${EXCLUDE_FROM_BOARD} virtual fields), labels (the column headers shown in the CSV), group_by, sort_field, delimiters, exclude_dnp, and an optional extra_blank_columns list for fab-house templates that expect empty pricing cells.

altium._comment: Professional fab/assembly BOM format (matches the Altium reference template the user provided). Pricing columns optional via extra_blank_columns.

kicad_default._comment: Eeschema's default BOM columns plus the rich metadata fields (Description / Manufacturer / MPN) the engine now populates from parts_database.json — fully populated columns by default.

minimal._comment: Three columns only — useful for quick part-count summary.

verbose._comment: Every KiCad field + every common custom property. Use when populating the schematic with full manufacturing metadata.

fab_with_pricing._comment: Altium-style + empty pricing columns the user fills in after parts-house quote.

pcb_export._comment: Phase 18. kicad-cli wrapper for PCB manufacturing files (Gerbers + drill + pick-and-place). Universal — works for any .kicad_pcb. Add/remove layers in `gerber_layers` to control what gets plotted; never hardcode in code.

schematic_preview._comment: Phase 9. Auto-export an SVG preview after every build so the chat can show the rendered schematic inline. Universal — takes any .kicad_sch path, no circuit-specific logic. Disable by enabled=false to skip the kicad-cli step entirely (useful if you don't have kicad-cli on PATH).

block_rect._comment: Dashed block-rectangle drawing policy for the single-sheet zoned layout. Padding controls breathing room around the tightest component bbox; min_size enforces a floor so sparse blocks (few components) don't draw a tiny rect next to a dense MCU block. `deoverlap` separates two block boxes that would otherwise draw on top of each other by clipping the shared edge to the midline of the gap between their components (contents are never clipped). Pure data-driven — no per-circuit logic.
block_rect._separate_comment: When two functional blocks' COMPONENTS physically overlap (not just their padded boxes), `deoverlap` alone can't fix it because it never clips contents. This pass runs BEFORE deoverlap/recenter: it pushes the whole overlapping block (all its components, rigidly) apart along the axis of least penetration until each pair of content bboxes has a clear `separation_gap_mm` between them. Fixes 'block on top of block' when a tall IC (e.g. ATmega) overflows its zone cell into a stacked neighbour. Grid-snapped; bounded by separation_max_iters. Disable for legacy output.

text_placement._comment: Reference/Value field placement, pin-side aware — reproduces the reference 'name above, value below; keep text off the wire' convention. Text goes on the body edge that carries NO pins: parts with pins on left/right (ICs, regulators, diodes, horizontal passives) get RefDes centred ABOVE + Value centred BELOW; vertical 2-pin passives (R, C, L with pins top/bottom) get RefDes+Value stacked to the RIGHT, left-justified, clear of the through-wire. gap_mm = distance from body edge to text; line_gap_mm = half the vertical spacing between the stacked ref/value of a side-placed part. Set enabled=false to fall back to each symbol library's own field offsets (legacy, byte-stable). Set vertical_side_placement=false to keep the above/below rule for verticals too.
text_placement._comment_avoid_pin_columns: Nudge a body-centred RefDes/Value horizontally so its text box clears any vertical pin-stub column on that edge (an IC power pin exiting top/bottom drops a wire straight down through the centred Value — the 'value sits on the wire' defect). Steps in 50-mil increments toward the shorter shift; clearance_mm is extra gap each side of the text box; max_steps bounds the search (if pins span both sides wider than the text the field stays centred, no worse than before). Set avoid_pin_columns=false for byte-identical centred placement.

combine_sheets._comment: Safety thresholds for the combine_sheets tool. `max_combined_components` refuses merges that would produce too-large a sheet (industry-standard EDA recommendation is to KEEP hierarchy for designs past 25-30 components per sheet). `require_shared_net` blocks merges of sheets with no electrical bridge between them (combining unrelated circuits onto one page just clusters them — doesn't connect them). `lateral_gap_mm` is the horizontal gap between adjacent merged source blocks.

cross_block_guard._comment: Phase 0.2 (BMS roadmap). Stops two DISTINCT signals silently shorting via same-named GLOBAL labels across sibling sheets. THREE independently-revertible layers. The DEFAULT cure is Layer C (proactive prompt rule, ON): the architect gives every inter-block signal a globally-unique descriptive name, so no collision ever forms. Layers A and B are OPT-IN safety nets (default OFF) because a generic name spanning two blocks is fundamentally ambiguous — a 2026-06-11 adversarial review showed a bare 'ALERT'/'RST'/'EN' is OFTEN a LEGITIMATE single shared signal (e.g. BQ76952 ALERT -> MCU), so flagging/renaming it by name alone produces false positives. Enable A/B per-project only after a golden BMS fixture validates them.
cross_block_guard._validate_collision_check_comment: Layer A — a heuristic post-merge LINT (warning) that flags a non-power net spanning >=2 blocks whose name matches weak_signal_name_patterns. OPT-IN (default false): a merged IR has no per-block origin to prove intent, so on a real BMS this flags legitimate shared signals as noise. Turn on only as a diagnostic.
cross_block_guard._weak_signal_name_patterns_comment: Anchored regexes for BARE BUS-INDEX tokens only (D5/A3/IO7/GPIO2/Q1/Y0) — the canonical 'each block has its own D0..D7' accidental-collision shape. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES functional signal names (ALERT/RST/RESET/EN/INT/FAULT/RDY/READY/...) AND protocol buses (SPI*/I2C*/UART*/CAN*/SCL/SDA/MOSI/MISO/TX/RX): those are commonly LEGITIMATE single shared signals across blocks, so renaming/flagging them by name is wrong. A descriptive name (MCU_BQ_ALERT, CAN_TX) never matches -> Layer B unions it (connection preserved), never splits it. Tighten/loosen here, never in code.
cross_block_guard._splice_rename_incidental_comment: Layer B — the structural guard in block_repair.splice_block. When a regenerated block net's name matches an existing net that is NOT a declared boundary, neither side is a power rail, AND the name matches weak_signal_name_patterns (so it is a bare bus-index, almost never a deliberate shared signal), RENAME it instead of unioning. The weak-name gate is what makes this safe: a descriptive emergent shared signal is unioned, not split. DEFAULT OFF until a BMS golden fixture validates it.

chat_ui._comment: Status-banner wording shown during a chat turn. Professional EE/PCB-engineering vocabulary (replacing the generic 'Thinking...'). Edit either string here to re-word without touching server.py — restart the chat server to pick up changes.

heartbeat._comment: Keeps the chat WebSocket alive during long (multi-minute) circuit builds. Between the build_circuit tool_use and its tool_result no frames flow, so the socket sits idle for minutes; uvicorn's keepalive or the client then drops it, and the finished build (file already written) is lost because the reply + eeschema-reload never get sent. This sends a real frame every interval_seconds during idle gaps so the socket stays warm and a dead client is detected within one interval. enabled=false restores the plain async-for loop (byte-stable).
heartbeat.text: Still working — generating the schematic ({elapsed}s elapsed)…

thinking._comment: Stream the model's real reasoning to the chat as a collapsible 'Thinking' panel (Claude.ai-style), replacing the fake rotating 'Analyzing/Designing' label. budget_tokens>0 uses fixed-budget extended thinking (--max-thinking-tokens N) — the classic mode supported by ALL thinking-capable models incl. the default Haiku 4.5, so it is the safe default. Set budget_tokens=0 to use 'adaptive' instead (model decides depth; needs an adaptive-capable model like Opus 4.7+). display 'summarized' returns Anthropic's summarized thinking (recommended), 'omitted' returns none. enabled=false => no thinking events emitted, byte-identical to before. Restart the chat server after changing.

page_summary._comment: Page-scoped on-open summary cards. When the chat panel opens, server.py reads the current file (.kicad_sch for the eeschema panel, .kicad_pcb for the pcbnew panel) and emits a `page_summary` WS event using these templates. NO LLM call — purely deterministic. All wording lives here so a project can re-tone the greeting without code changes. Disable by enabled=false (server then sends NO page_summary on hello and the chat starts blank like before). DISABLED 2026-06-23: in the unified single-window shell the shared AI panel re-hellos on every tab focus flip (schematic<->pcb), so app_ctx flips, the per-connection dedupe key changes, and a new card is emitted each time -> the chat spams repeated 'Current PCB' / 'Current schematic' context cards + 'Open PCB' buttons (no frontend dedupe). Turned off to stop the noise; re-enable once emission is project-scoped (dedupe key without app_ctx) + frontend renders only the first.

detection._comment: Pattern rules the deep schematic analyzer uses to classify components. Pure data — add a new regulator family or MCU vendor by appending to the list, no Python edit. Matches are case-insensitive regex against the component Value (and lib_id for connectors/crystals).

voltage_extraction._comment: Exact-match value-string -> output-voltage map. Substring fallback handled in code. Add new lines as new regulators show up.

detection._regulator_voltage_suffix_comment: Last-resort heuristic: extracts a trailing voltage number from the value string. Catches families like 'AP7361-XX' where -XX is the voltage code. Disable by setting to empty string.

confirm_buttons._comment: Chat-panel confirmation buttons (server.py emits a `confirm_buttons` event after each assistant reply that matches one of `triggers`). The 'Ask' button was removed 2026-05-25 — it duplicated the text the assistant already wrote. Re-add an entry to `options` to bring it back, or extend `triggers` to fire the button bar on additional preview cues.

validate._comment: Project-level IR validation thresholds. canonical_power_rails is the allowlist used when validate.py inspects net names; non-canonical names raise POWER_RAIL_NONSTANDARD warnings. Add to this list (don't fork the Python code) if your project uses non-standard rail names like +VBAT_PROT or +3V3_ANALOG.

connectivity_guard._comment: BOARD_UNDER_WIRED guard. Rejects a board that was returned as a parts list without wiring (architect emits nets=null on ~100-part boards). Fires only when components >= min_components AND the fraction of component pins wired to any net < min_pin_coverage. Conservative defaults: a normal board wires 60-90% of pins, so 0.25 catches only the never-wired case. Set enabled=false to disable.

pin_role_check._comment: PIN_ROLE_MISMATCH guard (2026-06-08). The architect chooses each net's pin refs as free strings; with no pin catalog for a part it can hallucinate the pinout (observed on ATmega328-P: VCC<->GND swapped, the crystal/RESET nets landing on GPIOs while the real XTAL/RESET pins were left no_connect). The engine resolves refs by EXACT name/number and renders the wrong pins faithfully, and ERC stays silent because a GPIO is still 'connected'. This guard rejects two unambiguous datasheet-role violations at the IR gate (fires `error` so the architect-retry loop regenerates): (1) a ground-named power pin wired to a +V supply rail or a positive-supply pin wired to GND (VCC/GND swap); (2) a net NAMED for a dedicated function (XTAL1/XTAL2/RESET) landing on a pin OTHER than the part's dedicated pin for that function. Conservative by design: only clearly-named power pins and explicitly function-named nets are checked, so V-/VEE/VREF and arbitrarily-named nets never false-trip. Set enabled=false to disable. Token lists are tunable here (no Python literals).

normalize._comment: IEC 60062 value normalisation + KLC label conventions. Each list lives here so a project can extend (e.g. add custom refdes prefix 'NTC' for a thermistor family) without code edits. differential_pair_prefixes drives the active-low override (signal_P / signal_N pairs are NOT inverted). unit_by_refdes_prefix maps the refdes letter to the SI unit used during value normalisation. refdes_categories is the ASME Y14.44 prefix -> category map used for BOM grouping and refdes validation.
normalize._comment_resolve_lib_ids: Correct hallucinated IC lib_ids against the real symbol libraries, keyed on the part VALUE (MPN). The architect names the part right in `value` ('BQ76952', 'INA240', 'STM32G474VET6') but often guesses a wrong/fake lib_id -- a wrong library ('Sensor_Battery:BQ76952' vs the real 'Battery_Management:BQ7695201PFBR') or a different real part ('Amplifier_Operational:TL072' for an INA240). A wrong-but-valid symbol loads with no error then every real pin wired onto it fails PIN_NOT_ON_SYMBOL, and the repair loop grinds for minutes on an unfixable mismatch (the BMS build's #1 hard failure). normalize_ir resolves each IC (refdes 'U', or any component whose lib_id won't load) to the best VALUE-matching symbol across ALL libraries via symbol_geom.resolve_lib_id_by_value. resolve_lib_ids_margin = how much better the found symbol must score than the current one before an already-loadable id is replaced (broken ids are always replaced). Set resolve_lib_ids false to revert.
normalize._comment_normalize_block_names: Map an unregistered architect block name onto the closest REGISTERED name (config/block_naming.json:blocks) BEFORE validate, so a descriptive name ('MCU_CORE', 'CURRENT_SENSE', 'LOAD_CONTROL') doesn't hard-fail as BLOCK_NAME_NOT_IN_REGISTRY and spin the repair loop. FULLY DYNAMIC + per-circuit-agnostic: scores each registered name by token overlap against the block's own name AND its block_type (regulator/sensor/analog/mcu/comm/driver/io/...), exact match preferred, renames to the best only if it clears block_name_match_min_score. No synonym table (block_name_aliases is an empty optional override). Set false to revert.

refdes_prefix_aliases._comment: Informal / vendor refdes prefixes mapped onto their ASME Y14.44 letter. Applied in normalize_ir BEFORE validation, renaming the component AND every site its ref appears (net pins, block membership, anchor pins). A rename that would collide with an existing ref is skipped (keeps the original + its warning). KiCad's default switch prefix is 'SW' -> ASME 'S'. Extend freely (e.g. 'LED':'D', 'XTAL':'Y') with no code edit.

tie_nets._comment: Groups of net names that are the SAME electrical node in this design family (first entry = canonical). When a single pin bridges two nets in the same group (the PIN_IN_MULTIPLE_NETS symptom), normalize renames both to the canonical rail so they collapse into one net. A pin bridging nets NOT in any group is left as a hard validation error (real wiring bug). Default empty = nothing auto-merges. Add e.g. ["+3V3","VBAT"] only for boards where VBAT really is tied to +3V3 (no coin-cell backup).

normalize._comment_merge_floating_connector_rails: Deterministic safety net for the two architect slips that dominate multi-block MCU boards: (a) a BARE rail token used as a pin endpoint ('GND' with no dot) -> fires PIN_MALFORMED and strands the rail on two nets; (b) a single-pin '*_GND'/'*_VCC'/'*_3V3'/'*_5V'/'*_VBAT' connector net (UART_GND, SD_VCC) the architect forgot to fold into the global rail -> fires NET_FLOATING. Each has exactly ONE correct resolution (the named global rail), so normalize folds it in instead of bouncing the architect through a retry. Ambiguous *_VCC/*_VDD nets are only merged when the board has exactly ONE non-ground power rail. Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_resolve_multinet_passives: Deterministic resolution of PIN_IN_MULTIPLE_NETS on 2-TERMINAL parts (R/C/L/ferrite/diode), where a pin on two nets is always an architect slip (never a legit dual-role pin -- those live on multi-pin ICs). The fix is decided by whether the part's OTHER pin is already wired: OTHER PIN FREE -> MOVE the functional net to it (R5.2 on [GND,LED_PWR] with R5.1 free -> R5.1=LED_PWR, R5.2=GND), polarity-free parts only so a diode/electrolytic is never flipped; OTHER PIN WIRED -> DROP a redundant membership (drop the net equal to the other pin's net -- which would short the part end-to-end -- else drop the canonical power rail, keeping the functional node: C17.1 on [+3V3,VCAP_1] with C17.2=GND -> drop the spurious +3V3). 3+ net pins, both-rail ties, multi-pin devices and unloadable symbols are left for the validator, so this only ever removes a real error and never creates a short. Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_merge_net_aliases: Deterministic merge of two nets that share >= 2 physical pins -- they are the SAME electrical node under two names (NRST + SWD_NRST both holding the reset pull-up pin AND the SWD header reset pin; the dominant slip on the STM32F405 CAN-logger build). Two pins shared on two names is always one node (no legit topology lists the same two pins on two nets -- that shorts them at two points). Sharing exactly ONE pin is the ambiguous bridge case left to resolve_multinet_passives. Two DISTINCT power rails sharing pins are NOT merged (a real short -> validator). Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_global_pin_ownership: GLOBAL one-net-per-pin guarantee (_enforce_pin_ownership), run DEAD LAST after every merge/tie/resolver above so the invariant holds on the FINAL net set. A physical pin is one electrical node, so a pin on >1 net is always wrong. The merge test is PURELY STRUCTURAL -- no net-name heuristics, no power-token lists, nothing circuit-specific: it merges two of an over-assigned pin's nets only when they are literally the same name OR share 2+ physical pins (a two-point tie can only be one node). A single shared pin is the ambiguous bridge (CAN_H/CAN_L) and is NOT merged. Pin identity is resolved from the LIVE symbol (a name in one net == a number/alias in another), so it is fully dynamic and part-agnostic -- no per-part table. Genuinely-distinct nodes (a real architect mis-wire onto two different rails, or rail+signal) are LEFT for the validator + repair loop; this never blind-drops a membership (that could silently mis-wire the board), only merges same-node nets. Default true; set false to revert (byte-identical: the pass is skipped entirely).
normalize._comment_unified_multinet_resolver: When true, ONE classify->act resolver (_resolve_pin_multinet) handles ALL of PIN_IN_MULTIPLE_NETS -- it replaces the scattered ground-fold (merge_shared_pin_ground_nets) + shunt-fold (fold_shunt_tap_aliases) + 2-terminal drop/move (resolve_multinet_passives), which are skipped when this is on. For each pin on >1 net it classifies by the part + what its OTHER terminal touches, then MERGEs (one node: ground alias, or a shunt tap whose names are both-power or related-signal), DROPs (series part's redundant membership / decoupling cap's spurious rail), MOVEs (symmetric bridge to a free terminal), or leaves it (REVIEW), iterating until stable. Same guards as the scattered path (GND never folded into, two distinct rails never merged, unrelated signals never merged, diodes never pin-swapped) so it never shorts. Default false = keep the proven scattered path; flip true to use the consolidated resolver (passes every multinet/net-repair/complex regression suite at 0 shorts).
normalize._comment_fold_shunt_tap_aliases: Deterministic merge of two nets that meet at the SIGNAL pin of a SHUNT 2-terminal part (TVS / filter / decoupling), recognised because the part's OTHER pin lands on GND or a power rail. A shunt part TAPS a node, it does not separate it, so a pin double-listed on [MAIN, MAIN_alias] is one node -> fold the alias into the canonical/more-connected name (D2.A on [CAN_H, CAN_TVS] with D2.K on GND -> CAN_TVS folds into CAN_H; C3.1 on [+5V, J4_PWR] with C3.2 on GND -> J4_PWR folds into +5V). This is the dominant ATTEMPT-1 PIN_IN_MULTIPLE_NETS on multi-block boards (a protection/decoupling part tapped onto a bus under a second descriptive name). Conservative: only when the other pin is provably on GND/rail; never merges two DISTINCT rails; the SERIES case (other pin on one of the two signal nets, e.g. an LED series resistor) is left to resolve_multinet_passives' DROP rule. Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_fold_intent_named_stubs: Completes a SINGLE-PIN net whose NAME encodes a rail intent by renaming it to that rail so the by-name merge folds in its lone pin and finishes the leg the architect left open: *_PU/*_PULLUP -> dominant logic rail (a pull-up returns to VCC), *_PD/*_STRAP -> GND (pull-down / boot strap returns low), *_VDDA/*_AVDD -> dominant logic rail (analog supply stub). This is the DOMINANT residual on large data-logger boards (self-test 2026-06-06): the architect declares NRST_PU / SD_DET_PU / BOOT0_PD and leaves it floating (NET_FLOATING), or splits the analog supply onto a VDDA_RAIL stub AND lists VDDA on +3V3 too (PIN_IN_MULTIPLE_NETS). Conservative + non-destructive: fires ONLY on a single-pin non-power net carrying an intent TOKEN ('_'-delimited, not substring) and only when the target rail already exists -- a single-pin net is already a hard error so folding it can only remove errors, never short. Token->rail map overridable at intent_stub_targets. Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_intent_stub_targets: Override map for fold_intent_named_stubs: net-name TOKEN (uppercase) -> rail kind ('vcc' = dominant logic rail, 'gnd' = board ground). Inline fallback: PU/PUP/PULLUP->vcc, PD/PDN/PULLDOWN/STRAP->gnd, VDDA/AVDD/VREF->vcc. Add a token (e.g. 'VBACKUP':'vcc') with no code edit.
normalize._comment_merge_shared_pin_ground_nets: Deterministic resolution of PIN_IN_MULTIPLE_NETS where a SINGLE physical pin sits on BOTH the global GND and a derived '<BASE>_GND' bus/connector ground reference (CAN_GND, RS485_GND, LIN_GND, SHIELD_GND). The shared pin is a galvanic tie -> the two grounds are provably one node, so they cannot be isolated; on a non-isolated transceiver the bus ground reference IS the board ground (ISO 11898-2 requires the shared reference). normalize folds the '<BASE>_GND' net into GND so the by-name merge collapses them, instead of bouncing the architect through a non-converging retry (the lone recurring error on the STM32F405 CAN-logger: J4.Pin_2 on [GND, CAN_GND], 3 attempts failed). Bus-agnostic: any future '<BASE>_GND' folds with no code edit. Conservative -- fires only when exactly ONE of the pin's two nets is the canonical ground and the other is '<BASE>_GND'; deliberate split grounds (split_ground_bases) and 3+-net pins are left for the validator. Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_split_ground_bases: Uppercase BASE names in a '<BASE>_GND' net that denote a DELIBERATE split ground (analog/digital/power/chassis/earth) joined to GND only at a single star point -- these are NEVER auto-folded by merge_shared_pin_ground_nets. Everything else ('<BASE>_GND' where BASE is a bus/connector name) is treated as a ground reference common with GND. Extend per project (e.g. add 'ISO' for an isolated section's ground) with no code edit.
normalize._comment_complete_power_tree: Completes the power tree a DEGRADED architect attempt left open (the 21x POWER_PIN_FLOATING wreck), without guessing the ambiguous parts. (a) Synthesises a GND net when missing but ground pins exist, so the floating-ground tie has a target. (b) For each voltage REGULATOR (lib_id matches regulator_lib_markers) ties its floating power_OUT pin to the rail its part number defines (AMS1117-3.3 -> +3V3, LM2596S-5 -> +5V, LM7812 -> +12V), creating that rail net if absent -- the regulator is the authority on its own output rail; an adjustable/unparseable reg is skipped (no guess). It ALSO guards _tie_floating_power_pins so a regulator's INPUT pin is never auto-folded into the logic rail (that upstream rail is a design decision; folding it would short input to output). Strictly additive -- only wires currently-floating pins. Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_regulator_lib_markers: Uppercase lib_id substrings that mark a voltage regulator for complete_power_tree. Inline fallback ['REGULATOR'] (covers KiCad Regulator_Linear / Regulator_Switching).
normalize._comment_power_input_pin_markers: Uppercase substrings in a PIN name marking a board power INPUT/source (USB VBUS, barrel-jack/regulator VIN) that _tie_floating_power_pins must NOT fold into the logic rail (its upstream voltage is a design decision; folding would short input to output). Inline fallback ['VBUS','VIN'].
normalize._comment_tie_floating_power_pins: Tie any IC power_in pin absent from every net to the correct rail (ground-type names -> GND; supply names like VDD/VCC/VBAT/VDDA -> the dominant logic rail by connector_vcc_rail_priority). Mirrors the validator's POWER_PIN_FLOATING check, clearing it every build instead of via retry. Only power_in is auto-tied; a floating power_out (regulator output) is handled by complete_power_tree. Fires only when the target rail already exists. Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_tie_crystal_caps_gnd: For each crystal, tie each adjacent load cap's free (non-crystal) pin to GND -- mirrors the validator's CRYSTAL_LOAD_CAP_NO_GND check. Strictly additive: only grounds the cap pin when it is not already wired anywhere, so it never double-lists a pin or creates a short. Set false to revert.
normalize._comment_tie_floating_led_cathode: LEGACY per-component LED-cathode tie. DEFAULT FALSE -- superseded by the data-driven pin_completion engine (its 'led_cathode' rule does the same thing without dedicated code). Kept as a fallback only; leave false unless you disable pin_completion.
normalize._comment_complete_design_checklist: Turns the validator's detect-only design checklist into detect-AND-synthesise. validate._run_design_checklist DETECTS missing SHUNT support parts (MCU reset pull-up, LDO input/output caps, crystal load caps, USB-C CC pull-downs) for ANY part via the lib_id/pin-name patterns in design_checklist.json, but only reports them -- so that whole class bounces to the architect, which re-emits the FULL board and diverges on large designs (the CAN-logger retry storm). When true, intent/checklist_repair.complete_design_checklist reads the SAME config + consumes the validator's own issues and ADDS the missing part, wiring it from the offending pin's net to the rail/GND the checklist names, and assigns it to the supported part's block. Part-agnostic (acts on issue CODES, never part names), deterministic (no LLM/retry), strictly additive + short-free (shunt class only: a 2-pin part between an existing net and a rail/GND). SERIES insertion (LED current-limit R) and STRUCTURAL additions (a missing bus connector / SD socket) change topology and are LEFT to the architect. Runs LAST in normalize_ir so the rails it attaches to already exist. Default FALSE until live-verified; flip true + restart to activate.
normalize._comment_expand_verified_blocks: Phase 2 verified-block expansion (intent/verified_blocks.py). When true, after complete_design_checklist, normalize_ir instantiates any stored verified support sub-circuit (config/verified_blocks/*.json) whose anchor IC appears in the IR -- e.g. an INA240 current-sense front-end: shunt + input filter R's + diff filter cap + Vs decoupling + the datasheet internal wiring. GENERAL + config-driven: any anchor part can have a template, zero code. Internal net names are namespaced by the anchor refdes so two instances never bond via same-named global labels; support pins join the anchor's EXISTING V+/GND rails; the architect keeps the boundary (OUT->ADC, REF->bias). Strictly additive, never shorts, never raises; skip_if avoids double-injecting when the architect already wired the front-end. Default FALSE until live-verified; flip true + restart to activate.
normalize._comment_net_repair_vocab: Tuning knobs for the four structural net repairs above -- all part/circuit-agnostic, NO hardcoded part numbers. net_alias_min_shared_pins: pins two nets must share to be merged as one node (floored at 2). ground_pin_name_markers: substrings in a PIN name that classify it as ground for the floating-power-pin tie (substring match so VSSA~VSS, AGND/DGND~GND; any IC). power_pin_etypes: KiCad symbol electrical-types treated as a SINK power pin needing a rail (power_out excluded -- a source has no derivable rail). capacitor_refdes_prefixes: refdes letters that denote a load capacitor for the crystal-cap-GND repair. Crystal lib_id glob patterns are read from design_checklist.json:rules.crystal_oscillator.trigger_lib_id_patterns so repair and validation stay in sync.
normalize._comment_polarity_free_passive_prefixes: Refdes letter-prefixes whose parts are symmetric / polarity-free, so the multinet resolver may SWAP their pins (MOVE a net to the opposite pin). Diodes (D) and electrolytics (Device:C_Polarized, caught by polarized_lib_markers) are deliberately excluded -- swapping their pins flips the part. Config-driven; inline fallback {R,C,L,FB,RV,RT}.
normalize._comment_polarized_lib_markers: Uppercase substrings in a lib_id that mark a polarity-SENSITIVE 2-terminal part (electrolytic / tantalum). A match disables the pin-swap MOVE action for that part (DROP, which never swaps pins, still applies). Inline fallback ['POLAR'].
normalize._comment_ground_rail_aliases: Uppercase net names treated as ground when classifying logic vs ground rails in the connector-rail fold. Inline fallback {GND,AGND,DGND,PGND}.
normalize._comment_connector_vcc_rail_priority: When a generic '*_VCC'/'*_VDD'/'*_VBAT' connector net must fold into a rail and the board has MORE THAN ONE logic rail, pick the first of these (by priority) that is present -- a connector's VCC is the MCU logic rail, never the raw input or analog rail. Inline fallback [+3V3,+3.3V,+5V,+1V8,+2V5].

nc_policy._comment: Auto-emit (no_connect) markers on every unused pin so KiCad's ERC pin_not_connected check passes WITHOUT manual cleanup. Pure data-driven — covers any IC, any circuit, no part-number hardcoding. The pin etypes listed in auto_nc_etypes are the KiCad pin electrical types that ERC normally flags when left unconnected. Library pins already tagged etype='no_connect' are always covered. Set enabled=false to revert to the old 'only library-tagged NC pins' behavior.
nc_policy.skip_etypes_comment: power_in / power_out pins are NOT auto-NC'd — those should either be wired or fixed at the IR level. Output pins are also skipped — leaving them dangling is a real design error, not noise.

instance_unit_filter._comment: When true (default), NC markers are emitted ONLY for pins belonging to the instance's rendered unit + unit-0 (shared). Multi-unit symbols (LM358 / LM324 / LM2904) declare pins under sub-blocks `<name>_<unit>_<style>`; emitting NC on un-rendered units' pins puts X markers at coordinates that visually overlap the active unit. Filter: pin.unit in {0, instance_unit} -> eligible for NC; else skip.

hierarchy_layout._comment:
Dynamic layout for the parent (root) sheet in multi-sheet hierarchies. Picks the smallest page that fits all child-sheet boxes, then picks a grid (cols x rows) whose cell aspect best matches target_box_aspect, then sizes every box so they all fit AND avoid the title-block area at the bottom of the page. Pure data-driven — no hardcoded grids, no per-circuit logic. Change page_size_priority to bias toward A3/A2 sooner for large projects. Sheet boxes never overlap the title-block reserve.
`default_render_paper` is the paper used by simple flat renders (single IC, no blocks).
`single_sheet_with_blocks_paper` is used by multi-block circuits drawn on ONE sheet (POWER + MCU + OLED on one page) — A3 by default because the extra width fits the block columns without cramping.
hierarchy_layout._paper_priority_note: Page size auto-selected by `auto_paper` rules below when enabled. When auto_paper.enabled=false, falls back to default_render_paper (flat) / single_sheet_with_blocks_paper (multi-block).

auto_paper._comment: Dynamic paper-size selection driven by component count + block count. Universal — no per-circuit logic. Rules evaluated in order; first match wins. NOTE: the placer is page-agnostic today — it spreads components in a 30mm grid around sheet centre regardless of paper size. So picking A5 for a 7-component circuit with a connector is unsafe (the connector lands off-sheet). Until the placer becomes page-aware, A5 is reserved for tiny circuits (≤4 parts, e.g. RC filter / voltage divider). A4 covers everything else single-sheet; A3 takes block-heavy designs.
auto_paper._dynamic_block_fit_comment: When true (and the circuit has functional blocks), the paper is sized DYNAMICALLY from the actual block grid: smallest standard page (A5..A0) whose usable area gives every block its full un-shrunk zone (zone_w_mm x zone_h_mm from placement config), so block rectangles never overlap. Derived from the signal-flow grid span x ideal zone size — NOT a component-count threshold. The count-based `rules` below are the fallback for block-less (flat) circuits or when this is false.

hierarchy_layout._box_aspect_comment: Width / height ratio for each sheet box. ~1.3 = slightly wider than tall — leaves room on right edge for hierarchical pin labels.

sheet_pin._comment: Hierarchical-sheet-pin stacking geometry on the parent's sheet boxes. _compute_hierarchy_grid uses these to floor each box's HEIGHT so the busiest block's pins fit inside the box edge(s); _emit_sheet_box uses the same values to actually place the pins. Without this floor, a block touching many cross-block nets ran its pins off the box bottom and off the page (the hierarchy-sheet layout error). top_gap_mm = first pin inset below the box top; pitch_mm = vertical spacing between pins (2.54 = 100 mil); bottom_pad_mm = clearance kept below the last pin. distribute_both_edges: when true, pins beyond what one edge holds wrap onto the LEFT edge (so only half the count drives box height); set false to keep all pins on the right edge (taller boxes).

convert_to_hierarchy._comment: Phase 14b. Turn a flat .kicad_sch into a multi-sheet hierarchy. Components grouped by `default_prefix_blocks` (refdes prefix -> block name), or by user-supplied `blocks` mapping passed to the tool. Original is snapshotted via apply_ops_snapshots before re-render.

auto_layout_pcb._comment: P27 (2026-06-23). Closed-loop PCB layout orchestrator (tools/auto_layout_pcb.py). The pipeline IS this step list — re-order/disable/add steps here, no Python change. Each step dispatches to that tool's own @tool handler with the same pcb_path; per-step `args` merge over the tool's config defaults. stop_on_error halts on the first failing step (default false: run all, report each). The final step (pcb_verify) gives the board's end state. Runs AFTER footprints exist (F8 or pcb_gen).
auto_layout_pcb._repair_comment: Phase 4 of the Universal PCB engine (Fix 4, R10): close the loop. After the step list runs, read the DRC and route every still-unconnected net on route_layer, re-checking up to max_rounds (stops early when connectivity is clean or a round makes no progress). Connectivity repair is ADDITIVE — it adds tracks on the back layer and never moves placed parts. enabled=false (DEFAULT, SAFE) skips the loop. NOTE 2026-06-26: validation showed that on a congested all-THT board, the B.Cu connectivity additions (this + ensure_ground_return) can produce tracks_crossing/shorting under the loaded netclass clearance — keep OFF until that is isolated; enable per-board only on SMD/roomier boards.
auto_layout_pcb._steps_note: Canonical post-import pipeline (manual `auto_layout_pcb` runs ALL of these incl. route). set_design_rules (net classes + fab clearances), mounting holes and fiducials were added 2026-06-24 so the one-shot tool also writes design rules + fab features. The AUTOMATIC post-build finish (build_circuit) runs this same list but SKIPS the tools in pcb_gen.finish_skip_tools (default route_pcb_simple).

ampacity._comment: P26 (2026-06-23). IPC-2221 track-width-for-current engine used by tools/set_track_widths_pcb.py. A net is POWER if its name starts with one of power_net_patterns.patterns; otherwise Default. Each class has a design current; the required width = IPC-2221 area equation (A[mil^2]=(I/(k*dT^0.44))^(1/0.725), width=A/copper_thickness_in_mils) then optionally divided by ipc2152_factor (IPC-2152 allows narrower for the same current — keep 1.0 for conservative pure-2221). Under-sized track segments on a net are widened to its required width (only_widen never shrinks). net_current_a overrides a specific net by name. Verified: 1A/10C/1oz external -> ~0.30mm, matching the published IPC-2221 chart. All knobs here; nothing hardcoded in Python.

silkscreen_cleanup_pcb._comment: P25 (2026-06-23). DFM silk fix run by tools/silkscreen_cleanup_pcb.py and dispatched by drc_autofix for silk_overlap. Relocates each footprint's reference-designator / value silk text off its own pads to the nearest clear spot just outside the pad cluster.
