Every threshold here is config-driven — no constants in Python. text_fields selects which property names move (Reference only by default; add 'Value' to also move values). char_width_factor approximates the KiCad stroke-font glyph advance for the text-width estimate. gap_mm/ring_step_mm/max_rings define the outward search ring. hide_if_no_room hides text that cannot be placed clear (off by default — prefer leaving it visible and reporting).

drc_autofix._comment: Phase 19c2 + 2026-06-23 closed-loop rewrite. DRC violation -> PCB tool dispatcher with re-check + regression guard. Each strategy maps a DRC issue type to a PCB-mutating tool; disable per type by `strategies.<type>.enabled=false`; per-action `args` override what we pass to the dispatched tool. After applying, DRC is re-run and the board is restored from a byte snapshot if the total (errors+warnings) rises (regression_guard='on'). max_rounds>1 iterates while each round strictly reduces the total.
drc_autofix._regression_guard_note: 'on' = revert the .kicad_pcb to its pre-fix snapshot whenever a round raises the total violation count (errors+warnings). 'off' = keep whatever the fix produced (still re-checked and reported honestly).
drc_autofix._max_rounds_note: Default 2 = apply the phase-ordered plan, re-check, and run one more pass if it strictly improved (iterate-to-plateau). Each fix is kept only if it does not raise the total (per-fix guard), so more rounds never make the board worse. Raise to 3-4 for stubborn dense boards; the orchestrator may also pass this per call.
drc_autofix._guard_note: regression_guard 'on' = per-fix ERRORS-FIRST guard (snapshot -> run one fix -> re-DRC -> keep only if it did not ADD a hard error or swap in a new error-signature, else restore that fix). Warnings never block an error fix, so a re-route that clears a short but leaves a net unrouted (a warning) is still kept. This is why a clear+reroute that fails to fully reconnect can never undo the placement/pour fixes earlier in the same round. 'off' = apply every fix unchecked (fast, unsafe).
drc_autofix._signature_guard_note: ERC parity (mirrors erc_autofix.signature_regression_guard). When true, a fix is reverted if the error COUNT is unchanged but a brand-new error-signature (type@location) appeared — i.e. it swapped one error for a different one. When the error count DROPS the fix is accepted outright, so re-routes that move copper to new coordinates are never wrongly reverted. Set false for count-only behaviour.
drc_autofix._strategy_note: Each violation TYPE dispatches to the PCB tool that actually repairs it, applied in phase order (outline -> place -> route -> pour -> silk). Routing-caused copper errors (shorting_items / clearance / copper_edge_clearance / track_dangling) clear the bad copper and re-route clearance-aware via route_pcb_simple replace=true. Add/override here without touching code; set enabled:false to leave a type report-only.

unconnected_item._comment: Pour GND (fixes the bulk of unconnected GND pads). Unconnected SIGNAL nets are reconnected by the clear+reroute the routing-error types trigger on the same board.

shorting_items._comment: Two nets' copper touch. Clear the shorting tracks and re-route clearance-aware (replace=true wipes the bad copper first). Guarded per-fix.

clearance._comment: Copper-to-copper too close. A track-to-track clearance hit is fixed by a clean clearance-aware re-route; a pad-to-pad one is opened by the courtyards_overlap place-refine that runs in the earlier phase. Per-fix guard reverts if the re-route does not help.

copper_edge_clearance._comment: Track too close to the board edge. route_pcb_simple keeps an edge keepout; re-routing with replace=true pulls the offending track in.

track_dangling._comment: A track that does not reach a pad. Re-routing the net removes the stub.

starved_thermal._comment: A pad's thermal-relief spokes can't carry the connection. Re-pour the zones so the spokes are rebuilt.

solder_mask_bridge._comment: Two solder-mask openings merge. Usually adjacent parts too close -> spread them in place. Same-footprint pin bridges revert harmlessly under the guard.

courtyards_overlap._comment: Auto-fixable: dispatches to auto_place_pcb in refine_only mode, which pushes overlapping footprint courtyards apart in place (no re-gridding). Also resolves the clearance/mask errors that the same overlap produced.

silk_overlap._comment: Dispatches to silkscreen_cleanup_pcb to nudge the reference text clear of pads/copper.

erc_autofix._comment: Phase 19b + 2026-05-27 rewrite. Incremental ERC repair: each proposal applied in isolation, re-validated against kicad-cli, rolled back if it INCREASED the error count. Replaces the old bulk-apply that cascaded errors (6 -> 19 regression). Strategy fixes: PWR_FLAG now spirals outward from the error coord to find a free spot (no more 'Power output and Power output connected' cascade); duplicate_reference uses next-free number (R1 dup -> R7) instead of '_dup' suffix; delete_wire uses tight 0.1mm tolerance so only the exact dangling stub is removed.
erc_autofix._verb_executors_note: Phase 3 (2026-06-09). Global kill-switch for the taxonomy's executor="verb" tier. When true, a safe_auto violation whose erc_taxonomy.json entry has executor="verb" is turned into concrete apply_ops (add_no_connect for pin_not_connected, snap_endpoint for endpoint_off_grid, delete_wire for wire_dangling) and applied — still confidence-gated by the taxonomy and re-validated by regression_guard below, so the schematic is never left worse. When false, those types fall back to diagnostic-only (the pre-2026-06-09 behaviour, byte-stable). Per-type opt-out: set that type's executor back to "diagnostic" in erc_taxonomy.json.
erc_autofix._result_as_json_note: When true (2026-06-08), erc_autofix returns its result as a JSON object in the tool's text block ({path, ops_applied, report}) instead of bare prose — so the server's KiCad auto-refresh path fires after a fix lands (it reads tool_result = json.loads(content[0].text) and reverts the open .kicad_sch via IPC, the SAME way build_circuit + apply_ops already do). `path` is non-null ONLY when apply=true AND >=1 op landed, so previews never trigger a needless revert. The full human report stays under `report` for the chat AI. Set false for the legacy bare-prose text (byte-stable, but NO auto-refresh after ERC fixes).
erc_autofix._regression_guard_note: Phase A (2026-06-08). HARD invariant: applying fixes must NEVER leave the schematic with more errors OR a new violation than it started with. Modes: 'batch' (DEFAULT) = apply all fixes, run kicad-cli ERC ONCE, and if the final report has more errors than baseline or any brand-new violation signature, restore the original file wholesale (1 ERC run, all-or-nothing, never worse); 'per_fix' = re-run ERC after EACH proposal and undo_last_edit only the offending fix (surgical, keeps good fixes, but 1 ERC run per fix = slow); 'off' = apply with no verification (fastest, unsafe). When this key is ABSENT the mode is derived from legacy validate_each_fix (true->per_fix, false->off) so old configs stay byte-stable.
erc_autofix._signature_guard_note: When true the guard compares the SET of violation signatures (type@x,y) before/after, not just the error COUNT. Catches 'swaps' (a fix clears error X but creates error Y at a different coord, leaving the count unchanged) and 're-introductions'. Set false for pure legacy count-only behaviour.
erc_autofix._hierarchy_aware_note: Phase H (2026-06-09). For a MULTI-SHEET project, kicad-cli groups violations under `***** Sheet /NAME/` headers and the @(x,y) coords are LOCAL to that child sheet. When true, erc_autofix maps each violation to the child .kicad_sch that owns it (via the parent's (sheet ...) refs) and applies the fix THERE at the already-local coords, with a per-file batch snapshot/restore. When false (or for a flat/single-sheet design with no child sheets), every violation resolves to the parent path = the legacy single-file behaviour, byte-stable. Fixes the bug where PWR_FLAG/no-connect flags landed on the parent canvas at child-local coords (connected to nothing -> original errors unfixed + new '#FLG Pin not connected' errors). FLAT and SINGLE_SHEET_BLOCKS render to ONE file so they were never affected; only HIERARCHY needed this.
erc_autofix._validate_note: LEGACY flag, kept only as the back-compat fallback used when `regression_guard` is absent (true->per_fix, false->off). Superseded by `regression_guard` above, which wins whenever present.

unconnected_wire_endpoint._tol_note: Tight tolerance so only the wire whose endpoint is EXACTLY at the reported coord is removed. The legacy 1.27mm value was wide enough to delete a perfectly-good wire that happened to terminate one grid cell from the stub.

power_pin_not_driven._note: Re-enabled 2026-05-27 after PWR_FLAG placement was made collision-aware (_find_clear_flag_pos). Each flag now spirals outward from the floating pin until it finds a coord with no neighbouring symbol within 5mm — avoids the old cascade where the flag landed on top of another pin.
power_pin_not_driven._trace_note: trace_before_flag (2026-06-01): when true, erc_autofix calls trace_net to find the real root cause BEFORE adding a PWR_FLAG. already_driven -> propose nothing (a flag would mask a wire/label continuity bug); missing_wire (exactly one orphan power_out exists) -> draw the wire instead of a flag; no_driver -> PWR_FLAG fallback. Set false to restore legacy PWR_FLAG-first behaviour for every error.

apply_ops_snapshots._comment: Phase 20. Before every apply_ops call, the tool copies the current .kicad_sch into <sch_dir>/.envil-snapshots/<basename>.<ts>.envil-bak.kicad_sch so destructive edits (delete, reroute, rename) can be undone. The `undo_last_edit` verb restores from the most recent snapshot. Retention: oldest snapshots beyond `max_snapshots` are auto-deleted.

hierarchy_edit._comment: Cross-sheet edit routing for HIERARCHY designs. In a KiCad hierarchical project the parts live on child sheets and the root .kicad_sch is just (sheet ...) stubs, so a ref-based edit ('delete R2') can't find its target on the root. When enabled, the snapshot reader aggregates every sheet's components (each tagged with its owning 'sheet' file) and apply_ops routes ref-targeted edits (delete/move/rotate/change_value/change_footprint/set_property/set_dnp/add_decoupling) to the child sheet that owns the ref, then writes that file back. Pure FALLBACK: a ref that exists on the primary file is handled exactly as before, so FLAT and SINGLE_SHEET_BLOCKS designs are unaffected. Default on.

rename_net._comment: rename_net verb config. `power_lib_prefix` is the lib_id prefix used for power-port symbols in the user's KiCad library (default `power:`). Most KiCad installations use `power:GND`, `power:+3V3` etc. — if your project uses a custom library like `Project_Power:GND`, change this string and the verb will follow. `label_node_heads` lists the s-expr head names that represent signal-net labels — extend if you use custom label flavours.

pullup_pulldown_defaults._comment: Defaults for add_pullup / add_pulldown verbs when the user / agent doesn't specify them. Tune here per project — no per-circuit hardcoding in code.

apply_ops_defaults._comment: Fallback values for apply_ops verbs when the user/agent omits a field. Everything is read from here so NO value is hardcoded in tools/apply_ops.py; user-supplied op fields always win. pullup/pulldown/led/decoupling have their own *_defaults sections — leaving those op fields blank lets THOSE sections drive the result (the dispatch must pass blanks through, not literals).

led_indicator_defaults._comment: Defaults for the add_led verb (indicator LED = series resistor + LED + ground port, fully wired from a GPIO pin). Tune here per project — no per-circuit hardcoding in code. Topology: source pin -> R -> LED anode (pin 2/A), LED cathode (pin 1/K) -> rail. value is the series-resistor value; color goes into the LED's Value field.

multi_block._comment: Multi-block circuit upgrade (Phase 1-4). Controls when the engine takes the zoned-placement path (each block placed in its own region) vs. the flat-placement path (single global anchor + satellites). Single-IC circuits (NE555, LM317, op-amp) must continue to use the flat path — those work well today and any change here must not regress them. The architect prompt is responsible for emitting blocks=[] for single-IC circuits; this config is the engine-side guard.
multi_block._rule: REFERENCE-SCHEMATIC RULE (user-confirmed 2026-05-21): (1) INSIDE a block — components connected by WIRES (R1→C3 in RESET, LDO→caps in POWER, MCU→C6 in MEMORY). (2) MCU pin → other block — LABELS at MCU pin tip + matching label at destination (UART_TX, SPI_SCK, SWDIO etc). (3) Power rail across blocks — LABEL + power-port symbol per block (each block has its OWN local VDD power port; NOT a drawn bus). Defaults below enforce this rule: flow_dag ON (left-to-right block ordering), decoupling ON (caps adjacent to IC VDD pin -> within-block clusters get wires via existing power-net cluster logic), interblock_wires OFF (drawn inter-block wires CONFLICT with the rule that inter-block connections use labels + power ports).
multi_block._hierarchy_global_pwr_flag_comment: DEFAULT true. Hierarchy-wide PWR_FLAG synthesis. When true, render_hierarchical builds ONE global rail-driver registry over the whole design (every block) and shares a flagged-rails set + #FLG counter across all child sheets, so each power rail gets AT MOST ONE PWR_FLAG, with a globally-unique #FLG reference, and NEVER on a rail already driven by a native power_out in ANY sheet. Fixes the per-sheet defect where every child restarted at #FLG001 (=> 'Duplicate items #FLG001') and dropped a flag on a rail driven by the regulator in another sheet (=> 'Pins of type Power output and Power output are connected'). Fully dynamic — decisions come from pin etype + the net graph, never from a net name / refdes / part type. Set false to restore the legacy per-sheet behaviour (byte-stable).
multi_block._allow_partial_zoning_comment: When true, a genuine multi-IC board still uses zoned (block-by-block) placement even if some blocks are passive-only (e.g. a CLOCK block of crystal + load caps that owns no >=3-pin part). Without this, ONE passive block used to force the WHOLE circuit onto the flat single-anchor path, scattering every block's parts into one ring so the block rectangles overlapped page-wide. Gated by zoned_min_anchored_blocks so circuits that aren't really multi-IC (0-1 anchored blocks) keep the flat path.
multi_block._cross_block_signal_wires_comment: Phase 4b. Enforces the reference rule 'INSIDE a block use WIRES; BETWEEN blocks use LABELS'. When false (default), signal-net pin pairs whose owners belong to DIFFERENT IRBlocks are NEVER wired — only labels carry the connection. When true, the body-aware router decides per-pair (legacy behavior; allows cross-block wires whenever a clean L-path exists). Rule is purely IR-data-driven (block membership), so flipping this knob never depends on IC names, circuit names, or any hardcoded list.
multi_block._cross_sheet_label_kind_comment: Multi-SHEET (hierarchy) cross-sheet connection model. Applies ONLY to render_hierarchical (parent + N child sheets), not to the flat single-sheet path. 'global' (default, Model B): a cross-block signal net emits a (global_label) at each pin in every child it touches — KiCad bonds same-named global labels across ALL sibling sheets automatically, no parent wiring needed. Parent sheet boxes carry NO sheet pins in this mode. This is the standard model for a flat sibling hierarchy (every sheet a direct child of one root). 'hierarchical' (Model A): emits (hierarchical_label) in children + matching (sheet_pin) on each parent box — the strict parent/child interface. NOTE: Model A is only electrically complete once render_hierarchical ALSO draws parent-side wiring joining same-named sheet pins across boxes; that parent-wiring pass is NOT implemented yet, so 'hierarchical' currently leaves sibling cross-sheet nets open. Power rails are unaffected by this knob — they always go via global power-port symbols.

mcu_centric_layout._comment: Phase 5 (2026-06-02). 2-D MCU-centric block placement for MCU boards. Anchors the MCU/controller block at the sheet centre and places every other block in a compass cell around it (power top-left, clock top, reset top-right, connectors right, output bottom — from the canonical layout.zone_layout map). UNLIKE flow_dag's 1-D column grid, cells are sized to each block's ACTUAL estimated content (content-aware), so a tall MCU (e.g. ATmega328P = 76mm) never overflows a fixed-height row into a stacked neighbour — the structural cause of block-on-block overlap. ADDITIVE: consulted BEFORE flow_dag inside _place_components_zoned; returns {} (falls back to flow_dag, then ZONE_LAYOUT) when disabled or when there is no single dominant MCU/controller block (ambiguous / non-MCU board), so single-IC and multi-IC-non-MCU circuits are unaffected. Reversible — set enabled=false to restore the flow_dag path.
mcu_centric_layout._center_note: A block becomes the centre only if its block_type is one of center_block_types (or its anchor lib_id matches a flow_dag compute pattern) AND its anchor has >= center_min_anchor_pins. Excludes big connectors (Conn_02x20 = 40 pads) from being mistaken for the MCU. If two candidates tie on pin count the layout is treated as ambiguous and bails to flow_dag.
mcu_centric_layout._gap_note: Blocks are JUSTIFIED across the usable sheet: the inter-block gap grows to fill free space (so the design uses the whole page, not a cramped top-centre patch), clamped to [min_block_gap_mm, max_block_gap_mm]. The gap also shrinks toward min when the grid is too big. min guarantees boxes never touch; max stops a sparse board from flinging blocks into the far corners.
mcu_centric_layout._reserve_title_block_cell_comment: DEFAULT false. Reserving the bottom-right cell (1,1) exiled a connector to an extra far-right column (2,1), making the sheet look lopsided. Instead the reflow's title-block lift-up moves any block off the title block while keeping it in its normal column. Set true only if you'd rather leave (1,1) empty than lift.

relative_cell_map._comment: Landscape-optimised compass cells around the MCU at (0,0). col=left/right, row=up/down. Spreads power/clock/reset across the TOP row and connectors down the RIGHT column so blocks don't stack 3-tall in one column and overflow a landscape A3 (the screenshot's POWER/RESET/CLOCK-all-on-the-left bug). Matches the reference: POWER top-left, CLOCK top-centre, RESET top-right, MCU centre, comm/IO right, output bottom. Edit here to retune positions — no code change.

mcu_centric_layout._size_note: Each block's cell = the DRAWN rectangle size = max(anchor_bbox + 2*(satellite_depth per ~4 satellites) + 2*block_rect.padding_mm, block_rect.min_size). Cells are spaced by block_gap_mm of clear whitespace. To fit the page the engine compresses ONLY that whitespace (down to min_block_gap_mm), never the box size — scaling the box shrank the cell but not the actual symbols, so the full-size rectangle spilled into the neighbour and the boxes TOUCHED. min_block_gap_mm is the guaranteed clear air between any two block boxes (they never touch). If the boxes alone exceed the page the board is too dense for one sheet -> it's the >5-block hierarchy tier and never reaches this path.

flow_dag._comment: Phase 2b. Compute left-to-right block ordering from signal flow (power source on the left, compute in the middle, sinks on the right) instead of the static block_type → (col,row) map at engine.py:ZONE_LAYOUT. ENABLED by default — matches the reference convention (POWER top-left, MCU center, peripherals on right). When ir.blocks<2 the DAG is empty and the dispatcher falls back to ZONE_LAYOUT, so single-block circuits (NE555, LM317) are byte-identical to before. Block-level override: IRBlock.flow_role from the architect wins over component-based detection.

block_type_to_role._comment: Fallback default when IRBlock.flow_role is empty AND no power-input connector / regulator / MCU is detected in the block's components.

role_lib_substring_patterns._comment: Lib_id substring matches for inferring block flow_role from components (lowercase). Pattern matching is 'pattern in lib_id.lower()'. Per [feedback_no_hardcode_json_config]: replaced the in-code 'usb_c' / 'regulator_' / 'atmega' / 'stm32' literals that were originally hardcoded into _classify_role. Add a new family (esp32-c6, nrf52840, MAX1745) by editing JSON — no Python change. Priority order is source > regulator > compute > sink, so a USB-input block with an MCU on it still classifies as source.

decoupling._comment: Phase 3. Post-pass that moves decoupling caps adjacent to their target IC's power pin (instead of leaving them in a generic 'passives' cluster). Detection: 2-pin cap on (positive-power-net, GND) where the positive-power net also touches an IC pin (component with ≥3 pins). ENABLED by default — this is THE key change that delivers the 'INSIDE-block wires' part of the rule: once caps sit adjacent to the IC's VDD pin (<12.7 mm), the existing power-net cluster logic in render_flat groups them into ONE cluster, emits ONE shared power-port symbol, and draws wires from each cap pin to the IC pin. Runs ONLY in the zoned path (multi-block); defensive guard refuses to run when ir.blocks is empty, so single-block circuits (NE555, LM317) are unreachable by this code and remain byte-identical.
decoupling._apply_to_flat_single_block_comment: When true (default), the decoupling-cap relocator ALSO runs for flat single-block circuits (ir.blocks==[]). Without this flag, single-IC outputs (ATtiny85 dimmer, NE555 oscillator) left decoupling caps wherever the flat placer dropped them — sometimes 60+ mm from the IC's VDD pin. With this flag the relocator uses the tighter `child_sheet_max_distance_from_vdd_mm` threshold (default 8 mm) so the cap snaps next to the IC. Set false to revert to the byte-identical pre-2026-05-26 behaviour for circuits whose hand-tuned single-IC layout is preferred.
decoupling._row_layout_comment: Datasheet D1 'comb' drawing standard (user-chosen default 2026-06-02): lay each IC's decoupling caps in a ROW (perpendicular to the power pin's outward axis), +V pin facing the IC. Pairs with LOCAL power-port symbols (engine.single_block_power_cluster_radius_mm=3.81) so each cap pin gets its own +V/GND symbol instead of a shared bus -> renders fully clean (0 short / 0 overlap), textbook comb layout. The user explicitly preferred this over the prior 'wires INSIDE block' rule for power nets. Set false (and radius back to 0) to restore shared-bus wiring inside blocks.
decoupling._robust_destack_comment: Fix (2026-06-02) for the +3V3<->GND SHORT class: when two decoupling caps target the SAME IC power pin (e.g. a 100nF HF + a 10uF bulk cap, both 'Device:C'-prefixed), the de-stack collision loop must land them on DISTINCT coordinates. The old loop diffed a drifting `placed_bboxes` list by float equality, so the 2nd cap often did NOT see the 1st cap's just-committed position and stacked exactly on top of it (identical coord) -> the +3V3 and GND power-port wire clusters merged into one net = dead short. When true, the resolver instead rebuilds its collision set from the LIVE positions of every other placed component (keyed by ref) and verifies-after-snap (walks outward, then the perpendicular axis) so two caps on one pin can never end co-located. Set false to revert to the pre-fix byte-identical behaviour.
decoupling._text_aware_spacing_comment: Fix (2026-06-02) for cap field text overwriting neighbours (user: 'letter ellam overwrite aakuthu konjam space vittu'). The de-overlap pass used to fire only when two caps' BODIES overlapped, so a row of caps ~7.62 mm apart had clear bodies but the side-placed Reference/Value of one cap printed over the next cap / the +V rail label. When true, de-overlap measures each cap with a TEXT-INCLUSIVE bbox (body + the placed field reach: vertical caps grow on the right by the wider of ref/value at 50-mil font; horizontal caps grow top+bottom by field_stack_allowance_mm) and spreads caps until that clears. placed_bboxes still tracks body-only boxes, so non-cap layout is unchanged. Set false to revert to body-only de-overlap (byte-identical).
decoupling._field_stack_allowance_comment: Vertical reach (mm) added above AND below a name-above/value-below part (horizontal caps/ICs) when text_aware_spacing is on. 2.54 = field gap (1.27) + half a 1.27 mm text line, enough to clear a stacked cap's value-below from the next cap's reference-above. The right-side reach for vertical 2-pin caps is computed per-part from the actual ref/value string width, so only this top/bottom margin is a constant.

crystal._comment: R2.5 (2026-05-27). Post-pass that moves crystal-like 2-pin parts to the midpoint between the two IC pins they bridge — implements rule 'Keep crystal close to MCU pins'. Universal detection (no refdes / lib_id hardcoding): 2-pin part wired into 2 non-power nets where BOTH nets land on the same multi-pin IC. Catches crystals, ceramic resonators, differential filters. Threshold `min_anchor_pin_count` defaults to 8 (skips small ICs to avoid false positives — 2-pin filter caps between op-amp pins don't qualify). max_distance_from_pins_mm = if the part is already within this many mm of the midpoint, don't move it.

interblock_wires._comment: Phase 4. CONFLICTS WITH THE REFERENCE-SCHEMATIC RULE (see _rule above) and is therefore SHIPPED DISABLED. The rule says inter-block connections use LABELS + per-block power ports, NOT drawn wires. This phase exists as opt-in for a different aesthetic (visible bus across the sheet) — flip enabled=true only if you explicitly want drawn wires between blocks. Defensive: routes that pierce non-endpoint bodies are dropped silently (the label-net still carries the electrical connection either way). GND-like nets are skipped by default. Only runs when ir.blocks is non-empty AND the dispatcher took the zoned path — single-block circuits are unreachable by this code.

discrete_templates._comment: Phase 5. Topology-template placer for discrete-only circuits — bridge rectifier, voltage divider, RC filter, common-emitter amp, LED + current-limit resistor, H-bridge. Triggered ONLY when (1) ir.blocks is empty AND (2) no component has ≥ min_anchor_pin_count pins (no IC anchor) AND (3) the IR matches a known topology. Single-IC circuits (NE555, LM317) have ICs → topology detection returns None → fall through to existing flat path → byte-identical to today. Multi-block circuits have ir.blocks → unreachable. Enabled by default because the regression guard is strict — only discrete-only circuits without a known topology match see any change.

voltage_divider._comment: Phase 5b. Two resistors in series with a middle tap on a non-power node. Top resistor between Vin (power net) and middle tap; bottom resistor between middle tap and GND. Detection requires exactly 2 Device:R components forming this topology. chain_pitch_mm must keep R1's bottom pin and R2's top pin WITHIN the engine's 12.7 mm power-net cluster radius so they form ONE shared label + wire instead of two duplicated labels. With chain_pitch_mm=5.08, body-to-body gap is ~2.54 mm and the midpoint pins cluster.

power_net_patterns._comment: A net is treated as power if (a) any member is a power-port symbol (lib_id starts with 'power:' or refdes starts with '#PWR') OR (b) its name matches one of these prefixes (case-insensitive). Both checks are needed — bare wires labeled '+3V3' without a power-port symbol still need power treatment.

ignored_refdes_prefixes._comment: Refdes prefixes that represent annotation/utility symbols, not real components. Excluded from the connectivity graph so they don't inflate degree counts or create phantom nodes.

importance_weights._comment: score = w_pins * pin_count + w_degree * unique-non-power-neighbors + w_betweenness * betweenness_centrality. The highest-scoring node is the layout center candidate (MAIN_CONTROLLER). Tune these to bias toward pin-rich ICs vs hub-like passives.

edge_rules._comment: How non-power nets create edges between components. Power nets are excluded by default so the graph reveals signal topology (otherwise every component connects via GND and the graph is useless for layout). min_pin_count_for_edge filters single-pin dangling nets that would create no real edge anyway.

label_stub._comment: R13 (stub before label) + R11 (label collision avoidance) from WIRING_RULES.md. `length_mm` is the base stub from pin tip to label anchor. When a new label's anchor would land within `min_separation_mm` of a previously-emitted anchor on the same outward axis, the stub auto-lengthens by `stagger_step_mm` until separated (up to `max_stagger_count` times). Body-pierce guard: when an obstacle list is supplied, the stub endpoint must not land strictly inside any obstacle bbox; if it does, the stub is extended by `body_pierce_extend_step_mm` until it exits, capped at `body_pierce_max_tries`. Wire-overlap guard (R11-wire, added 2026-06-01): when an `existing_wires` list is supplied AND wiring_rules.r11_avoid_label_wire_overlap is true, the stub is lengthened by `wire_overlap_extend_step_mm` until the label text bbox no longer overlaps any previously-emitted wire segment.
label_stub._ink_comment: R11 unified text-bbox de-collision (added 2026-06-04, gated by wiring_rules.r11_unified_ink_decollide). After the per-label passes above, the stub is lengthened by `ink_overlap_extend_step_mm` (up to `ink_overlap_max_tries`) while the label's TEXT rectangle overlaps any committed ink -- component body+RefDes+Value (seeded at render start), other net labels, and power-port / PWR_FLAG names -- tested with `ink_overlap_margin_mm` clearance. Power ports lengthen their own stub by the same knobs. This is what stops long labels overlapping each other (VIN_FUSED), labels landing on RefDes/Value, and GND/PWR_FLAG names stacking.

pin_completion._comment: ONE data-driven engine (intent/pin_complete.complete_floating_pins) that connects a FLOATING component pin to its correct net -- instead of a Python function PER component (LED cathode, crystal cap, ground pin, ...). A floating pin's correct connection is its ROLE = (lib_id pattern) x (pin name / electrical type), so the knowledge lives HERE as data and one generic loop applies it. Adding a relay coil return, a Hall-sensor ground, an opto anode, a new MCU's VBAT = ONE rule below, ZERO new code. Each rule matches a pin by any of {lib_id_contains, pin_name_in, pin_name_contains, pin_etype_in} with optional guards (two_pin_only, require_other_pin_wired) and connects a matching FLOATING pin to connect_to (GND | DOMINANT_RAIL | explicit rail). First matching rule wins; list order = priority. 'Floating' = pin in no net OR lone pin on a single-pin NET_FLOATING stub. Strictly additive -- only touches pins the validator already calls floating. Set enabled=false to revert to the per-component functions.

load_completion._comment: ONE data-driven completion for a fully-floating 2-terminal LOAD / indicator (LED, buzzer, relay coil, motor, ...) -- NOT a function per part. A floating load needs a SOURCE on one terminal and a RETURN (GND) on the other; some need a series resistor. Each rule: lib_id_contains (which parts), source_pin / return_pin (matched by pin NAME or NUMBER), series_resistor (+resistor_value), source_to / return_to (GND | DOMINANT_RAIL | explicit rail). Fires ONLY when the load is fully floating (no real >=2-pin connection on either terminal) so it never touches a GPIO-driven or half-wired part. The source defaults to a power rail (safe always-on / always-energised completion, ERC-clean, unblocks the build; re-point to a GPIO afterwards). Adding a buzzer / relay / motor = ONE rule here, ZERO new code. Engine: intent/checklist_repair._complete_loads.

build_graph._comment: max_attempts raised to 3 (2026-06-02) so the validate->retry->architect edge can reach a clean IR and the full render->export path runs. detailed_trace=true selects the 7-node router_graph_detailed (classify_intent -> decide_render_mode -> architect -> normalize -> validate -> render -> export); set it false to revert to the 5-node router_graph. architect_timeout_seconds raised 45->180 (2026-06-04): on a large board (37-part STM32F405 CAN logger) the architect Claude call legitimately needs ~135s; the old 45s killed it every attempt -> APITimeoutError -> arun_with_retry re-ran the whole node -> retry storm (each pass ~270s, looped to max_attempts, GeneratorExit/no output). 180s lets a big board finish in one pass; small boards still return in seconds so this only raises the ceiling, never the floor.
build_graph._comment_single_build_trace: OBSERVABILITY. When true (default) the whole graph invocation runs inside ONE umbrella LangSmith run ('Build schematic'), parented to the turn's conversation ('Chat') run, so Plan blocks + every per-block Fix block + the engine spans nest into a SINGLE trace route instead of scattering as dozens of detached top-level rows. Needed because the Agent SDK invokes the build_circuit MCP tool in a task that does NOT inherit run_turn's run-tree contextvar, so without the umbrella each inner @traceable started its own root trace (the cluttered 'Fix block' list). Best-effort + fully wrapped: it never raises and never changes the build output. Set false to revert to the prior scattered-trace behaviour (byte-identical build).
build_graph._comment_architect_max_tokens: Output-token budget for the architect Claude call. Raised 4000->16000 (2026-06-05): 4000 could not hold a full ~100-part IR (components + nets). Because the strict emit_ir tool is grammar-constrained, an over-budget generation does NOT truncate visibly -- the decoder closes the JSON VALIDLY after the components array with nets=null, so the board parses fine but is completely unwired (the BMS build: 98 components, 0 nets). 16000 fits a ~100-part netlist with room to spare; small boards finish far under it, so this only raises the ceiling, never the floor. architect_block_max_tokens is the per-block (#9) call's smaller budget.
build_graph._comment_block_draw_attempts: Per-block draw retries in the incremental forward path (intent/incremental_build.py build_incrementally). A transient block-draw failure (180s timeout / Anthropic 529 / an over-budget block whose decoder closes the JSON empty) otherwise SILENTLY drops that block's whole intra-block wiring -> an under-wired board that validate can't catch (a dense monitor block's cell-sense pins are `input`, not power, so POWER_PIN_FLOATING / BOARD_UNDER_WIRED stay quiet). 2 = one cheap redraw recovers the common transient case; set 1 to restore the original single-attempt behaviour (byte-stable).
build_graph._comment_parallel_block_draw: PARALLEL BLOCK DRAW (incremental_build.build_incrementally). The incremental path draws each planned block in its OWN LLM call; by default those calls run one-after-another, so an 8-block board = 8 (x retries) sequential calls and a ~100-part BMS spent ~590s in 'Designing' then got CANCELLED past the ~9-min WS/timeout window before anything rendered (LangSmith trace 2026-06-12). The block DRAWS are independent (each block's interface is the PLAN's frozen boundary contract, and _reassert_plan_seams re-joins every cross-block seam afterwards), so when true they run CONCURRENTLY on a thread pool and only the SPLICE (which mutates the shared plan_ir) stays serial, in plan order -> wall-time collapses from sum-of-blocks to ~slowest-single-block. Each draw call builds its own Anthropic client (thread-safe) and the LangSmith @traceable parent context is copied into each worker so 'Fix block' spans still nest. DEFAULT FALSE (sequential path is byte-identical when off + on small/medium boards); set true to speed up large multi-block boards. parallel_block_workers caps concurrency.
build_graph._comment_graph_recursion_limit: LangGraph superstep ceiling for the build-graph ainvoke (tools/build_circuit.py). LangGraph's default is 25; a large board interleaving full regens (max_attempts) + per-block repair passes (max_block_attempts) can exceed it, crashing with an opaque GraphRecursionError that DISCARDS the keep_best IR. 60 covers the worst-case retry interleave with margin.
build_graph._comment_save_preview: SAVE-PREVIEW STAGE. When true (code default) the build graph ends with the preview/export node (router_graph 'preview' / router_graph_detailed 'Save preview') that runs _export_preview_svg over the parent + every child sheet, returns preview_svgs, and lets server.py push {kind:previews} to the chat for inline display. Set FALSE to drop the stage entirely: the node is never wired, so no SVGs are produced, the chat receives no previews, and the 'Save preview'/export span no longer appears in the LangSmith trace. Disabled 2026-06-05 at user request (image preview removed from the chat frontend; this also removes its backend half + LangSmith span). Flip back to true + restart to restore -- no code change.
build_graph._comment_keep_best_attempt: The architect retry can DIVERGE -- errors climb 5 -> 8 -> 27 across attempts and the last attempt drops whole power rails (21x POWER_PIN_FLOATING). When true (default): validate remembers the fewest-error IR, the retry loop STOPS as soon as an attempt has more errors than that best (no point burning the budget making it worse), and the terminal handler reports the BEST attempt instead of the last. Set false to revert to 'retry to max_attempts, return the last attempt'.
build_graph._comment_per_block_retry: PER-BLOCK RETRY (#9). When true AND the IR has blocks AND every current validate error localises to a block (none cross-block / global), the retry regenerates ONLY the failing block(s) -- the rest of the board stays BYTE-FROZEN -- instead of re-emitting all 37 parts (which diverges + times out on big boards). The LIVE detailed graph routes validate -> 'Fix block' (block_repair_node: localise -> _architect_block_call per failing block -> splice_block -> normalize_ir) -> validate, capped at max_block_attempts before falling back to a FULL architect regen. Only router_graph_detailed is affected (its _pass_or_fix); build_graph + the 5-node router are untouched. Default FALSE until live-verified; the offline splice core (intent/block_repair.py) is proven at 0 shorts. max_blocks_per_pass bounds how many blocks are regenerated in one Fix-block pass.
build_graph._comment_incremental_large_board: Forward 'draw bit by bit' generation for LARGE boards ONLY. When true AND the board's render-mode guess is in incremental_trigger_render_modes (hierarchy OR single_sheet_blocks by default -- generation is DECOUPLED from render mode as of 2026-06-09) AND the PLAN call's real count is >= block_repair_min_components parts, the architect node PLANS the blocks (one small skeleton call: components + blocks + rails + inter-block signals), then DRAWS each block in its own focused call and splices it into the growing board (intent/incremental_build.py) -- so a ~100-part board is never wired in one shot (which overflows the model's reliable output length and tangles cross-block, the BMS failure). Small + medium boards, and every RETRY, use the proven single-shot _architect_call unchanged. DYNAMIC + part-agnostic: the decomposition comes from the architect's own block plan for whatever board was asked, nothing per-circuit. Set false to revert to one-shot for all boards.
build_graph._comment_incremental_trigger_render_mode: DECOUPLES generation mode from render mode (fix 2026-06-09). Which pre-architect render-mode GUESSES are eligible to attempt the forward-incremental PLAN call. The PLAN call's REAL component count (>= block_repair_min_components AND >= 2 blocks, in architect._try_incremental) is the authoritative large-board decision; this list only pre-filters which boards pay the cheap PLAN round-trip, so a clearly-flat tiny circuit (render_mode=='', NE555 blinker) skips it. Was hard-coded to ['hierarchy'] only, which left a ~55-part board the keyword guess mis-tagged SINGLE_SHEET_BLOCKS on the lossy one-shot path (LLM drops nets) -- the large-board generation cliff. Added 'single_sheet_blocks' so any block-decorated board attempts incremental and the part-count gate decides. Add '' (flat/auto guess) to attempt incremental on EVERY board (full decouple) at the cost of a PLAN call on small boards.
build_graph._comment_max_builds_per_turn: HARD per-turn cap on build_circuit calls. The agent (Haiku) ignores the system-prompt's 'call build_circuit at most once per message' rule and re-invokes it 3-6x on a hard board, turning ONE failed build into a 600s+ no-output disaster (observed live: CAN logger via chat WebSocket, 6 calls / 676s / no schematic). The (max+1)th call this turn is short-circuited INSTANTLY (no architect loop) with a STOP message telling the agent to report the prior result. A prompt rule can't enforce this; this is the deterministic layer. Default 1; set 0 to disable.
build_graph._comment_block_repair_min_components: LARGE-BOARD GATE for per_block_retry. Per-block (decomposition) regeneration only kicks in when the board has >= block_repair_min_components components (OR >= block_repair_min_blocks blocks when that is > 0). Below the threshold a failed board routes to the normal full-architect regen -- unchanged, proven behaviour for the small/medium boards that converge single-shot (the data-loggers at ~34-37 parts). The threshold exists because the size-specific failure (one-shot ~100-part netlist degrading via output-length ceiling / context rot / lost-in-the-middle) is what decomposition fixes; small boards don't need it and shouldn't pay its per-block-call cost. 40 sits just above the data-logger size that converges single-shot; raise/lower to tune which boards decompose. Set block_repair_min_blocks > 0 to also trigger on sheet count.
build_graph._comment_feedback_available_pins: CLOSE THE PIN FEEDBACK LOOP. When true (default), a PIN_NOT_ON_SYMBOL validation error also carries the FULL real pin list of the offending symbol (read live from the .kicad_sym library -- no curated list, works for any part) plus a symbol-derived 'did you mean' ranking, and the repair prompts (per-block _architect_block_call AND the full-architect retry feedback) render an 'AVAILABLE PINS' section so the architect picks the actual library pin instead of re-emitting the hallucinated one (the BMS 'Vref/NRST/BOOT0' re-hallucination loop). The legacy truncated prose (first 8 pins) stays byte-identical; this only ADDS structured fields + the prompt section. Set false to revert to the exact prior behaviour (no extra issue keys, repair prompts unchanged).
build_graph._comment_mark_run_failed_on_validation_e: OBSERVABILITY. When true (default), a terminal build failure (validation errors after the retry budget, a graph crash, or a hard state error) sets the live LangSmith run's status to ERROR (red) with build_failed/issue_count/attempt metadata, so a build that produced NO schematic stops showing GREEN in the trace. It does NOT raise and does NOT change the friendly chat reply -- the tool still returns its is_error dict and the agent still synthesises its plain-English options. Best-effort + fully wrapped: it can never break a build. Set false to leave failed runs uncoloured.
build_graph._comment_fail_on_block_skip: Never ship an incrementally-SKIPPED block as a green success. When true (default), a genuine draw/splice FAILURE in the incremental forward path (block_interface raised, block_draw returned nothing after block_draw_attempts, or splice_block raised -- NOT an intentionally-empty plan block) is stamped on the IR and raised by validate as INCREMENTAL_BLOCK_SKIPPED, keyed to the block so the per-block repair loop redraws it (and prunes the mark on success). Without this an unwired block passes ERC silently (its input pins aren't power pins, so BOARD_UNDER_WIRED stays quiet). Set false to revert to the silent-continue behaviour (no IR stamp, no issue).
build_graph._comment_reset_attempt_on_full_handoff: Rescue the dead block->full handoff. When true (default), if per-block repair AND the architect attempt budget are both exhausted with errors remaining (and no hard error, and not a divergence-fail), the detailed graph routes once through a 'Retry full board' node that resets attempt + block_attempt to 0 (keeping the accumulated available-pins feedback) so a fresh full regen -- now armed with the real pin list -- can converge, instead of dying at max_attempts. Bounded by max_full_handoffs so it can never loop. Only router_graph_detailed is affected; set false and the 'reset' route + node are never wired (byte-identical routing).
build_graph._comment_max_full_handoffs: Hard cap on how many times reset_attempt_on_full_handoff may refresh the attempt budget in one build. 1 (default) = at most one extra full budget (worst case ~2x max_attempts architect calls, still under graph_recursion_limit). full_handoffs is never reset, so this is the loop backstop. 0 effectively disables the rescue even when the flag is true.
build_graph._comment_seam_reassert_ownership: PREVENT the incremental path from manufacturing PIN_IN_MULTIPLE_NETS. _reassert_plan_seams re-adds cross-block contract pins a block dropped during redraw. When true (default) it re-adds a planned pin ONLY if that pin is currently on NO net (genuinely dropped) -- a pin a block already wired elsewhere is NOT re-added, so one physical pin can never end up on two nets via seam re-assertion. When false, the legacy always-re-add behaviour (which blind-appends and can double-list a pin) is restored byte-identically. Pairs with normalize.global_pin_ownership (the post-assembly backstop).
build_graph._comment_offload_build_to_thread: Run the SYNC build graph in a worker thread (asyncio.to_thread) instead of blocking the asyncio loop with `await ainvoke`. The graph nodes are synchronous and the architect uses the sync anthropic client, so a ~6-min build otherwise freezes the loop -- nothing can stream to the chat or refresh eeschema mid-build (the heartbeat is the only thing that survives). Offloading frees the loop so progressive_status can push live per-block updates. to_thread COPIES contextvars, so LangSmith tracing keeps nesting under 'Circuit Design'. Default FALSE (the loop-blocking `await ainvoke` path, byte-identical) until live-verified; this is the prerequisite for progressive_status. Flip true + restart.
build_graph._comment_progressive_status: Stream a live 'Drew block 3/8: POWER' status to the chat as each block of a large incremental build is drawn, so the ~6-min build is not a black box. Needs offload_build_to_thread=true (else the loop is blocked and frames can't be sent until the build ends). The build worker hands each update to build_progress.emit(), which rides the SAME single heartbeat-queue consumer in server.py (no concurrent-send race). Default FALSE -> no per-block frames, the loop's consumer never sees a progress frame (byte-identical). Requires chat_ui.heartbeat.enabled (default true, the queue path).
build_graph._comment_partial_persist_on_failure: Don't throw away a large board that mostly built. When a build fails validation but drew some blocks cleanly, render+save the cleanly-drawn blocks (HOLDING OUT the broken/conflicted ones so the canvas is never electrically wrong) and report 'drew N, held out K: ...', instead of returning nothing. Held-out set = incrementally-skipped blocks + blocks owning unresolved errors (localize_issues). The partial is returned as a normal result with a `path`, so the server refreshes eeschema via its existing safe-revert. Only fires on the incremental (block) path. Default FALSE -> the legacy all-or-nothing failure text (byte-identical). Flip true + restart. ENABLED 2026-06-10 so a failed BMS shows its drawn blocks instead of a blank sheet.
build_graph._comment_plan_contract_complete: THE cure for floating cross-block control nets (NET_FLOATING on ALERT_NET / CFETOFF_NET / DFETOFF_NET / REGIN_NET / ...). In the incremental PLAN, the architect declares an inter-block signal on the source IC but often never wires the other end (the MCU GPIO), leaving a one-ended (floating) net that NO downstream repair can fix -- only the architect can decide which GPIO it lands on, and on a complex board it diverges trying. When true (default), after the PLAN call _complete_plan_contract DETECTS one-ended signal nets (non-power nets with <2 pins -- purely structural, no net-name table) and asks the architect to add the missing endpoint (it sees the board's real pins via the pin catalog), re-emitting the full plan BEFORE any block is drawn, so the both-ended contract propagates to both block draws and the net can't float. Bounded + only accepts a re-emit that reduces the one-ended count (never loops/regresses). Set false -> the plan is used as-is (byte-identical). The plan prompt also now always instructs both-ended signals.
build_graph._comment_plan_contract_max_attempts: Max plan-completion re-calls when one-ended signal nets remain (each is one extra ~cheap PLAN-sized architect call). 2 (default) is enough to complete the contract on a typical large board; raise if a very wide board still has one-ended nets after planning. Each re-call must make progress (fewer one-ended nets) or the loop stops early.
build_graph._comment_block_audit: PER-BLOCK correctness audit in the incremental forward draw (intent/incremental_build.py). After a block is drawn, validate IT IN ISOLATION (_audit_block builds a sub-IR of the block's components + internal nets + boundary rails) and, if it has block-fixable errors -- a pin name that isn't on the symbol (PIN_NOT_ON_SYMBOL), a power pin wired to nothing (POWER_PIN_FLOATING), or a pin on two of its own nets (PIN_IN_MULTIPLE_NETS) -- REDRAW that block with those errors fed back (block_draw renders the real available_pins), until it is clean or block_audit_attempts runs out. Catches the architect's per-block slips (e.g. INA240 'OUT' vs pin 5, STM32 'NRST', BQ76952 REG1/REG2/CP1 undecoupled, a GPIO put on two nets) at the BLOCK level where the model can fix them with focused context, BEFORE they pile onto the assembled board and diverge. Deliberately does NOT report NET_FLOATING in isolation (a boundary signal looks one-ended there but isn't). When true (default) the board is built block-by-block AND verified block-by-block. Set false -> a block is spliced as first drawn (byte-identical, single forward draw). Never raises; an audit failure just keeps the first draw.
build_graph._comment_block_audit_attempts: Max draws per block when block_audit is on (covers BOTH a transient draw failure and a correctness redraw). 3 (default): the first draw + up to two redraws with the audit errors fed back. Each redraw is one focused ~5-part block call (cheap + fast). Raise for a board whose blocks are dense/hard; lower to cap cost. A block that is still dirty after the budget is spliced as-is and the normal validate/repair loop downstream handles the residual.

auto_refresh._comment: Controls which schematic file(s) the server tells eeschema to reload after a build completes (server.py auto-refresh broadcaster). `active_only` (default, added 2026-06-01 per user request) refreshes ONLY the parent / target sheet the user had open --- hierarchical child sheets are produced on disk but not force-reloaded. `all_sheets` restores the legacy behaviour where every produced .kicad_sch (parent + children) gets a revert command sent to eeschema. Pick `all_sheets` only when the user routinely keeps multiple eeschema windows open at once.
auto_refresh._skip_open_comment: When true (default), the server does NOT send `open_file` to eeschema if the just-built file is already the schematic eeschema has open --- it sends only `revert` (in-place reload). `open_file` makes eeschema run a full OpenProjectFiles() which, on an already-open project, hangs on a hidden 'save changes?' modal and goes Not Responding (the 5-min freeze that forced a close+reopen). Set false to restore the always-send-open_file behaviour.
auto_refresh._touch_mtime_comment: When the target sheet is the one eeschema already has open, do NOT bump its file timestamp after a build. Touching mtime wakes eeschema's own 'file changed on disk - reload?' watcher, which races the in-place `revert` and leaves a pending modal that surfaces behind the close --- eeschema goes Not Responding and force-closing it leaves a stale .lck that re-triggers the freeze on the next open (the close+restart loop). build_circuit already wrote the file so its mtime is fresh; the touch on the active sheet is redundant. Sheets eeschema does NOT have open are still touched. Set true to restore the always-touch behaviour (only needed if reverts are being debounced).
auto_refresh._active_ignores_app_ctx_comment: When true (default, added 2026-06-05), a schematic eeschema has open is treated as the active sheet even if the edit arrived from the PCB editor (both windows open, PCB focused). The old logic required the message's app context to BE the schematic, so a PCB-context edit would touch+open_file the background schematic, arm its 'file changed on disk - reload?' modal, and hang the whole project when the user closed the schematic page. With both editors sharing one project lock, that bad close stranded the lock and made the NEXT file open from the project manager deadlock too. Set false to restore the app_ctx-bound behaviour.
auto_refresh._open_project_in_shell_comment: Cursor-style (2026-06-21, user: 'project folder create but not show in Project Files'). When true (default), after a build the server also broadcasts an `open_project` IPC message carrying the new project's .kicad_pro path. The single-window SHELL (KICAD_MANAGER_FRAME) has its own AI_IPC_CLIENT that handles `open_project` -> LoadProject(), which rebuilds the left 'Project Files' tree and resets its file watcher, so the just-built project's files appear (and update live) like Cursor opening a folder. Editors (eeschema/pcbnew) ignore the action; the shell skips the reload if it is already the active project. Without this the files land in F:/Ki_CAD/_envil_out/<name>/ but no open project is watching that folder, so the tree stays empty. Requires the shell IPC handler (kicad_manager_frame.cpp) — present from the 2026-06-21 fork rebuild. Set false to restore the editor-only refresh (no shell project switch).
auto_refresh._update_pcb_after_build_comment: Cursor-style fully-automatic F8 (2026-06-22, user: 'cursor type i need my ai automatic'). When true (default), after a schematic build the server broadcasts an `update_pcb_from_schematic` IPC message to eeschema, whose AI_IPC_CLIENT calls OnUpdatePCB(true). That opens/docks pcbnew (if needed) and applies the netlist SILENTLY (no Update-PCB modal) via BOARD_NETLIST_UPDATER with the dialog's default options, so footprints land on the board with zero manual steps. Requires the fork rebuild that adds the eeschema `update_pcb_from_schematic` dispatch + pcbnew silent-apply path (cross-probing.cpp MAIL_PCB_UPDATE payload=='auto' -> BOARD_EDITOR_CONTROL::UpdatePCBFromSchematicSilent). Set false to keep F8 manual (press F8 in eeschema yourself). Note: requires footprints assigned to the schematic symbols; symbols with no Footprint field are skipped by the updater.
auto_refresh._update_pcb_after_build_superseded: Set FALSE 2026-06-22: superseded by direct file-based PCB generation (see pcb_gen below + tools/build_circuit.py -> layout/pcb_gen.generate_pcb_from_ir). The board is now WRITTEN with footprints placed at build time (Cursor-style, no running-app F8), so the auto-F8 IPC broadcast is off. The eeschema/pcbnew silent-F8 fork path stays available as a dormant capability if you flip this true.
auto_refresh._refresh_pcb_editor_comment: Cursor-style live PCB sync (2026-06-25, user: 'editor refresh work file open and close time like cursor'). When true (default), after any PCB tool rewrites the .kicad_pcb (generate_pcb / auto_layout_pcb / route_pcb_simple / auto_zones_pcb / drc_autofix), the server broadcasts a `revert` IPC carrying the .kicad_pcb path so the open pcbnew silently reloads the board from disk — the same live-reload eeschema already gets for .kicad_sch. Requires the fork rebuild that adds pcbnew's `revert` AI-IPC handler (pcb_edit_frame.cpp: OpenProjectFiles + KICTL_REVERT, guarded to act only on the board it has open). Set false to restore manual File>Revert.

pcb_gen._about: Direct .kicad_pcb generation (2026-06-22, user: 'cursor type ... AI generates the .kicad_pcb directly'). After a schematic build, tools/build_circuit.py calls layout/pcb_gen.generate_pcb_from_ir(ir, sch_path): resolves each component's footprint, loads the .kicad_mod, grid-places it, assigns pad nets from the IR (symbol pin -> footprint pad via symbol_geom.resolve_pin), and writes a valid populated .kicad_pcb next to the .kicad_sch. No F8, no running KiCad app. Verified loadable by kicad-cli. enabled=false skips it (board stays the empty stub).
pcb_gen._finish_board_note: Master switch for the automatic post-generation finishing pass. When true (default), after generating the .kicad_pcb build_circuit makes the board follow the full professional rule set; false leaves the raw placed+netted board (no finishing). HOW it finishes is set by finish_via_auto_layout.
pcb_gen._finish_via_auto_layout_note: Upgrade (2026-06-24). When true (default), the post-build finish delegates to the config-driven auto_layout_pcb orchestrator and runs the FULL pipeline (set_design_rules/net classes, auto_place_pcb re-place + de-collide [block/IC-anchor, NOT the dumb refdes grid pcb_gen wrote], auto_outline_pcb, auto_zones_pcb GND pour, auto_thermal_vias_pcb, auto_mounting_holes_pcb, auto_fiducials_pcb, silkscreen_cleanup_pcb, drc_autofix, pcb_verify) minus finish_skip_tools. Before this, build_circuit ran a hand-rolled 3-step subset (outline + design_rules + ground_pour) on the dumb grid — skipping placement quality, thermal, mounting, silk and DRC, so generated boards ignored most placement/finishing rules. Set false to restore that legacy 3-step finish (results in summary.pcb.finished).
pcb_gen._finish_skip_tools_note: Pipeline steps the AUTOMATIC post-build finish skips (passed as auto_layout_pcb `skip`). route_pcb_simple: the simple Manhattan router can produce imperfect traces on a dense board, and GND is on the pour, so signal routing is left to the user / FreeRouting. drc_autofix + pcb_verify (added 2026-06-24): both shell out to kicad-cli DRC, which is slow and TIMES OUT on the freshly-generated (unrouted) board — running them inside build_circuit risks overrunning the build turn and giving the chat a false 'failed' result, and DRC on an unrouted board is low-value. The fast, high-value rule steps still run (placement, outline, net classes, GND pour, thermal vias, mounting holes, fiducials, silkscreen). Run drc_check / pcb_verify / auto_layout_pcb explicitly when you want DRC. Set to [] to run the full pipeline incl. route + DRC after every build.
pcb_gen._require_erc_clean_note: ERC-CLEAN GATE (schematic->PCB rule, 2026-06-22). When true (default), build_circuit generates the .kicad_pcb ONLY if the schematic has zero ERC errors after the self_heal autofix loop (count from final.erc_summary.errors, or a fresh kicad-cli ERC run when that's missing). With open errors it SKIPS generation and returns summary.pcb={blocked:'erc_not_clean', erc_errors:N} so the agent tells the user to fix ERC first — pushing an error-laden schematic to PCB would copy the mistakes onto copper. Warnings do NOT block (only errors). A checker failure leaves the count unknown and generation proceeds (don't fail the board on a tool hiccup). Set false to always generate regardless of ERC.
pcb_gen._fp_lib_table_note: fp-lib-table mapping footprint library nicknames to .pretty dirs. ${KIPRJMOD} in its URIs is substituted with kiprjmod_base; remaining ${VARS} resolve from the environment.
pcb_gen._lib_root_note: Fallback footprint root: when 'Lib:Name' is not found via fp-lib-table, pcb_gen looks for <lib_root>/<Lib>.pretty/<Name>.kicad_mod.
pcb_gen._placement_note: Initial grid: footprints grouped by refdes prefix, laid from (origin_x,origin_y) at pitch_x/pitch_y, `columns` per row, blank band between groups. auto_place_pcb or a future router can refine afterward.

readability._comment: Phase A layout-neatness pass (_readability_spread_columns). Default OFF -> output byte-identical. When enabled AND a placement has >= min_columns vertical columns (repeated 2-pin chains, e.g. an LED array), adjacent columns are spread apart so each column's field-text bbox PLUS net_label_reserve_mm (room for the net labels added later during routing) never overlaps its neighbour, leaving column_gap_mm of clear channel. Only ever INCREASES spacing and preserves each column's internal geometry, so chains stay intact. align_baseline shifts every column to a shared top baseline (the reference 'comb' look) -- default OFF because chains sharing a bottom rail (common GND) must not be misaligned.

electrical_integrity._comment: Correctness guards that outrank cosmetics (Phase C). All default FALSE so builds stay byte-identical until a project opts in. net_aware_junctions (C1): before add_missing_junction_dots dots a T-tap/meet, resolve the net identity of the wires (labels + power-port rails name a net; wires/pins/existing dots union connectivity) and REFUSE to dot any point that would merge two DIFFERENT named nets -- the 'two nearby circuits got interconnected' short. Withheld points + collinear cross-net overlaps are returned under cross_net_skipped for the build to flag / re-place. pin_completeness (C2): every pin of every placed symbol must be wired, labelled, on a power port, or explicit no-connect; anything else is reported (and auto-completed via pin_completion role rules where one matches).

wiring_rules._comment: Per-rule gates for the WIRING_RULES.md R-series. Each flag turns ONE engine-side enforcement on/off without code changes. Defaults chosen to preserve current behaviour: rules that have always been enforced default to true, rules added 2026-06-01 default to true once implemented but can be flipped off per project.
wiring_rules._r4_status: DETECTION only (via tools/audit_wires.py + lint.selectors.find_four_way_junctions). Auto-split mutator (lint.selectors.propose_four_way_split) exists but is NOT wired into the engine yet -- enabling this flag is currently a no-op.
wiring_rules._r4_add_status: ACTIVE: lint.repair.add_missing_junction_dots appends an explicit (junction) at every 3+ wire meet AND mid-span T-tap that lacks one (superset of r4_split_four_way). The T-tap case is a real connectivity REPAIR -- a wire ending on another wire's mid-span without a dot is electrically OPEN in KiCad. Never dots pure 2-wire crossings (find_missing_junction_dots excludes them), so unrelated nets are never merged. Idempotent; runs in repair_after_render.
wiring_rules._r9_status: IR support shipped (TopologyIR.buses + intent/bus_ir.py:BusDef); engine bus + bus_entry s-expr emission pending.
wiring_rules._r11_label_status: ACTIVE: _emit_label_with_stub lengthens stub when a new label anchor lands within label_stub.min_separation_mm of a prior anchor on the same outward axis.
wiring_rules._r11_wire_status: ACTIVE (added 2026-06-01): when existing_wires is passed to _emit_label_with_stub, the stub is lengthened until the label text bbox no longer overlaps any previously-emitted wire.
wiring_rules._r11_ink_status: ACTIVE (added 2026-06-04): one ink registry (_INK_RECTS) shared by every text emitter. Seeded with component body+RefDes+Value, then net labels and power ports lengthen their stubs until their TEXT rectangle clears all committed ink and register their own box. Replaces the point-distance, same-axis-only, body-only label check that let long labels overlap each other, labels overlap field text, and GND/PWR_FLAG names stack. Off -> nothing seeds/registers, _INK_RECTS stays empty, every consulting loop is a no-op and output is byte-identical to the legacy path. Tuning knobs live in label_stub.ink_overlap_*.
wiring_rules._r13_status: ACTIVE: every label goes through _emit_label_with_stub which emits a label_stub.length_mm stub between the pin tip and the label anchor.
wiring_rules._r11_text_status: ACTIVE (added 2026-06-08): lint.repair.clear_wires_over_text resolves the R11_TEXT warning (a wire running across a component's Reference/Value text). The router's obstacle set is body-only (_abs_outer_bbox), so it never avoided field text; this post-render pass nudges the obscured field anchor outward in r11_text_clear_step_mm steps (up/down/right/left, nearest-clear wins, up to r11_text_clear_max_tries) until its text bbox clears every wire + every OTHER component body. Moves ONLY the (property ... (at)) anchor -> connectivity byte-identical. Idempotent; byte-stable when no wire crosses a field. Set false to keep the legacy warn-only behaviour.

placement._comment: Engine-level placement tuning. `satellite_gap_mm` is the clear distance between an IC pin tip and the nearest pin of the radial satellite (cap / resistor). 2.54 = tight (was default), 5.08 = 2 grid cells, more visible breathing room for dense ICs like 74HC595 with many pins. The other knobs were previously hardcoded mm constants in engine.py module scope (ZONE_W, ZONE_H, CLEARANCE, power-cluster radius, spiral step) and have been pulled here so different circuit densities can tune them without code edits.

layout._comment: Block-type to (column, row) zone map used by the static-layout fallback in engine._zone_centre. Column 0 = anchor centre, -1 = left of centre, +1 = right; row -1 = above, 0 = same, +1 = below. Override per project to push specific block_types into custom zones without a code change.

routing._comment: L-aware Manhattan router tuning. `obstacle_detour_clearance_mm` is the gap left around a blocking component bbox when routing a Z-detour. `avoid_wire_crossings` makes the router rank L1 vs L2 by the number of other-net wires each path would cross — pick the option that crosses fewer (eliminates 'wire on wire' visual ambiguity). `max_wire_length_mm` caps signal-wire Manhattan length — paths longer than this are dropped and the per-pin label loop bonds the endpoints by name (professional convention: long wires across the sheet become labelled nets). 0 = no cap.
routing._avoid_wire_overlaps_comment: Fix (2026-06-02) for the +V<->GND SHORT class. _route_l_aware ranked L1 vs L2 only by perpendicular CROSSING count; a collinear OVERLAP (two different-net buses on the same line) was never penalised, so decoupling caps in a vertical column let the +3V3 cluster bus and GND cluster bus stack on one x-line and overlap = KiCad merges them = dead short. When true, the router (a) never takes the straight-line shortcut if it would lie on another net's wire, and (b) ranks L variants by (overlaps, crossings) so an overlap-free route always wins. Set false for byte-identical pre-fix routing.
routing._avoid_pin_shorts_comment: Fix (2026-06-08) for the FOREIGN-PIN mid-span SHORT class. _route_l_aware previously checked a path only vs component bodies and other-net WIRE segments — never vs a foreign PIN/PORT TIP lying on the segment's interior. A straight rail wire passing THROUGH an unrelated collinear pin (e.g. the GND backbone running through J1.Pin_1/+12V port, or the XTAL1 rail reaching the XTAL2 pin) makes KiCad mid-span-bond the nets = short, with no ERC trace of why. When true, the engine passes every component pin NOT on the current net as `foreign_pts` and the router rejects any straight/L/Z path whose interior crosses one (falling back to a dogleg, or to a name-bonding label if no clean route exists). Universal + geometry-only (no part names). Set false for byte-identical pre-fix routing.

engine._comment: Engine-wide render knobs that don't belong to a specific tool block. Tunable per project without touching Python.
engine._single_block_seed_label_when_clean_comm: When false (default, per user rule 2026-05-26 'single circuit wire tha use pannanum, not use label'), single-IC circuits where ALL signal-net wires routed cleanly emit ZERO signal labels — the schematic reads as direct wires throughout. KiCad auto-names the nets from connectivity. Set true to restore the legacy 'one seed label per net' behaviour (gives nets human-readable names like DISCH / TIMING in the schematic; pre-2026-05-26 behaviour). Multi-block circuits and circuits with dropped wires are unaffected — they always need labels to bond pins by net name.
engine._single_block_one_port_per_rail_comment: When true (default), single-circuit (no ir.blocks) renders use ONE power-port per rail regardless of how spread out the pins are — the engine wires every pin on that rail to the one port via L-routes. Eliminates the 'labels everywhere' look on flat single-IC schematics where the default 12.7 mm cluster radius produces 4–6 separate ports per rail. Per rule [feedback_wires_inside_labels_between]: single circuit = one logical block, USE WIRES.
engine._single_block_power_cluster_radius_mm_co: 3.81 (user-chosen 2026-06-02 = datasheet 'comb' layout, pairs with decoupling.row_layout=true): power pins farther apart than this radius each get their OWN local +V/GND power symbol + short stub instead of one shared bus. For decoupling caps laid in a row this puts a clean +V symbol on every cap's IC-facing pin and a GND symbol on the other — eliminating the shared-bus +V/GND OVERLAP that caused the board_four/five shorts and the cosmetic stacked-wire mess. Verified: MCU + regulator blocks render 0 short / 0 overlap; simple boards unchanged. SET BACK TO 0 (and row_layout=false) to restore the prior 'wires inside block, one port per rail' style.
engine._multi_block_one_port_per_rail_block_com: When true (default), multi-block renders use ONE power-port per (rail, block) regardless of distance within the block. Pins on the same rail in the same block wire to one shared port; pins on the same rail in DIFFERENT blocks land in separate clusters → separate ports per block → KiCad bonds them via net-by-label. Eliminates the per-pin power-port clutter that the 12.7 mm radius produced when a block's rail pins were spread 20–30 mm apart. Per rule [feedback_wires_inside_labels_between]: wires INSIDE block, labels (= cross-block ports) BETWEEN blocks. Set false to restore the legacy radius-based clustering.

sheet._comment: Sheet sizing. A4 landscape is the default for small/medium designs. When the role-grouped block count exceeds a4_block_limit, the placer auto-promotes to A3_landscape. margin_mm is the keep-out border on every side.

spacing._comment: Geometry constants used by the placer. component_pitch_mm is the per-cell pitch. block_padding_mm is the white-space ring inside a block's border. block_gap_mm is the lane between adjacent blocks. The per-cell label keepout pad is NOT specified here — it is DERIVED at runtime from label_format.fixed_font_mm and label_format.label_gap_mm (see _cell_size), so a single edit to those values propagates everywhere.

zones._comment: Sheet-fractional positions for each named zone (top-left corner of the zone's first block). A block assigned to zone Z lands at (frac_x * sheet_w + margin, frac_y * sheet_h + margin). Tuning these reshapes the whole sheet at once.

role_zone_map._comment: Legacy single-map fallback. Used when role_zone_maps is absent or the detected circuit type has no entry. New circuit types go in role_zone_maps instead.

circuit_detection._comment: Layer 5 classifier — picks a sheet-layout template from the role distribution after Layers 1-4 finish. Result: MCU_BOARD (default), POWER_SUPPLY, ANALOG, MOTOR_DRIVER, RF_CIRCUIT. motor_keywords is the substring match list against value + lib_id; add new motor-driver families with a one-line edit.

role_zone_maps._comment: Per-circuit-type zone layouts. The placer picks one of these maps based on circuit_type returned by Layer 5. Adding a new circuit type means: extend circuit_type.detect_circuit_type AND add a map here — no other code changes needed. Missing entries for a circuit_type fall back to MCU_BOARD's map.

MCU_BOARD._comment: Classic MCU-centric board: MCU center, power top, support circuits on the sides, connectors right.

POWER_SUPPLY._comment: Switching / linear PSU. Regulator at center, input protection top-left, output filtering on the right, connectors bottom.

ANALOG._comment: Pure-analog circuit (op-amps, audio, filters). The analog block anchors at center; passives spread around.

MOTOR_DRIVER._comment: Motor driver board. Driver IC center, power top, protection left, motor connector right, sense passives bottom.

RF_CIRCUIT._comment: RF / wireless module board. The radio module is the centre, MCU (if present) opposite, antenna connector to one side.

hide_pin_numbers._comment: Hide pin numbers + pin names on small symbols (≤ max_pins). A 2-pin diode rendering '1' and '2' next to a 2 mm body is pure clutter — net labels carry the connection info. ICs (>4 pins by default) keep pin numbers/names visible because P0.04 / VCC / GND on an MCU is genuinely useful. force_show_min_pins overrides any source-side `(pin_numbers (hide yes))` for symbols at or above the threshold — without this, an MCU lib_symbol cached with hide=yes from a foreign library renders without any pin numbers next to our column-aligned labels.

property_normalize._comment: After moving a component, override its Reference and Value property positions to KiCad's canonical convention: Reference centered above the body, Value centered below. The source schematic's property offsets may have been hand-tuned for a specific layout — when our placer moves the component into a tight zone those offsets often land the text on top of the body or on adjacent components. Disable (enabled=false) to preserve source offsets when emitting a near-pixel-perfect copy of the original schematic.

block_split._comment: Split blocks that have more than max_block_size members into multiple sub-blocks (e.g. a GENERIC trash bucket of 43 components becomes 3 sub-blocks of ~15 each). Sub-block role gets a `_N` suffix so the existing zone resolver pushes them into fallback zones with gaps. Universal fix for dense layouts — same logic helps dcdc's 127-component GENERIC.

bbox_padding._comment: Dynamic padding around the union-of-outlines bbox per block. Bigger blocks need slightly more breathing room than the constant in spacing.block_padding_mm provides — formula is `base + count * per_component`, clamped to [min, max]. Without this, dense blocks (many components -> tight bbox) get the same 5 mm padding as a 1-component block and look cramped.

debug_overlay._comment: Functional-zone overlay — circuit-shape gated. Dashed boxes + titles only render when they add navigation value: sheet must have ≥ min_blocks_for_borders distinct blocks AND ≥ min_components_for_borders parts AND ≥ min_distinct_subsystems distinct base roles. Per-block gate skip_single_component_blocks suppresses solo-part boxes; per-role floor `bbox_policy.role_min_members` suppresses single-IC PROTECTION/POWER_REGULATOR/CONNECTOR boxes that turn small datasheet-style circuits (LM317, AMS1117, NE555 reg-only) into 3-4 ugly dashed boxes. Industry rule of thumb (TI/ON/ST/KiCad/EMA/Cadence/Sierra/Schemalyzer): boxes are for MEDIUM+ circuits — small circuits (<20 parts, 1-2 sub-systems) render direct-wire single-sheet, no boxes.

bbox_policy._comment: Per-block bbox decision. always_box_roles get a box ONLY when they reach role_min_members[role] (or default_min_members if absent) — a lone U1 LM317 with role POWER_REGULATOR is not a 'sub-system boundary', it's the whole circuit. never_box_roles never get a box. Other roles: boxed when ≥min_components_to_box members AND title not in skip_topology_titles.

net_name_sanitizer._comment: KiCad rejects '(' and ')' in label names (KLC says label names must be a single symbol token). Auto-generated 'Net-(REF-PadN)' names from build_sheet_nets always violate. This rewrites the canonical auto-name shape to 'REF_PN' and strips remaining invalid chars from anything else. Applied at router emission time so routed.json carries clean text downstream.

connector_edge_placement._comment:
Post-placement pass that snaps CONNECTORS (lib_id starts with one of `connector_lib_prefixes`, OR refdes starts with one of `connector_refdes_prefixes`) to the sheet edge their function dictates. Inputs go LEFT, outputs RIGHT, debug headers BOTTOM-RIGHT. Detection is by NET-NAME PATTERN (regex against the names of nets the connector touches) — pure data, no part-number knowledge. Universal across NE555, LM317, op-amp, MCU, anything with a connector.

Matching rule: walk every net the connector pin-touches; first pattern that matches in priority order (left -> right -> bottom_right) wins. If nothing matches, leave the connector where the placer put it. Pattern syntax = Python regex, case-insensitive, anchored with ^...$ unless you write your own anchors.
connector_edge_placement._inset_comment: Distance from sheet edge to the connector's origin. Default 18 mm leaves room for pin-1 label + an outward power-port symbol.
connector_edge_placement._snap_only_comment: Skip snapping when the connector is ALREADY within this distance of its target edge — avoids jittering a connector the placer already got right. 25 mm = roughly the inset + one grid step.
connector_edge_placement._min_components_comment: Skip edge-snap on small flat single-IC circuits (< N components and no blocks). Otherwise a 7-part LDO has J1/J2 thrown to opposite sheet edges, +VIN/+VOUT become 250 mm spans, the L-router can't route them, and the whole sheet collapses to label-only bonding (per feedback_wires_inside_labels_between: small flat circuit = one logical block, use wires not labels). Set 0 to always snap.

power_port_edge_anchor._comment: Pattern from professional reference schematics: every block's positive-rail (VCC/VDD/+3V3/+5V) power-port symbol gets anchored to the block's TOP edge; ground-rail (GND/VSS/AGND) power-ports to the BOTTOM edge. A connecting wire runs from each colocated component pin up/down to the relocated port. Universal — relies only on rail-name polarity + block bbox geometry, no part-number knowledge. Disable for the legacy 'port-at-pin-tip' behaviour.

label_format._comment: Fixed-font label format. Net labels render as PURE net names — never embed the pin number into the label text. KiCad's native pin-number rendering on the lib_symbol covers visible pin-number display next to the body, and embedding a pin number into the label name produces invalid net identifiers (KiCad reports 'Lbl Bad Format' when labels start with digits / contain spaces). The embed_pin_number flag exists for experimental/visual-only use; default OFF so the chat's lint passes and labels stay valid net identifiers.

label_placement._comment: Dynamic label position resolver — try 4 orthogonal angles (outward + 2 perpendiculars + opposite), ray-cast each, first clear position wins. component_body_margin_mm pads each component bbox to cover ref/value text overhangs that aren't in the body bbox itself (KiCad renders 'Reference' + 'Value' properties ~2.5 mm outside the body line). Stub wire from pin tip to label is orthogonal-only; diagonal angles are rejected because KiCad parser rejects diagonal wires. spatial_hash_cell_mm controls the grid spacing of the O(1)-lookup index — bigger cells = fewer buckets but more candidates per bucket; 20 mm is a sweet spot for A4-class sheets.
label_placement._font_height_mm_note: auto-synced from label_format.fixed_font_mm at runtime; this fallback applies only if label_format is absent

dense_pin_stagger._comment: Superseded by swim_lanes. Set enabled=false; the old tier-by-index logic forced every Nth pin to a different lane even when adjacent pins fit fine in the same column.

column_alignment._comment: Per (component, unit, side) group: align every label's anchor to the same X (for left/right sides) or same Y (for top/bottom). Force swim-lanes when label count > max_column_labels even if pin pitch is technically OK — a 26-label single column still reads crammed visually even at 2.54 mm pitch.

swim_lanes._comment: Fallback when column_alignment is disabled. Greedy lane assignment per (component_side, outward_angle): each label assigned to first lane with enough vertical clearance; opens new lanes as needed.

hierarchical_split._comment: Step 6: hierarchical sheet splitter — circuit-shape-driven. Fires when ANY of: (1) min_main_controllers MCUs are present (multi-MCU board); OR (2) component count ≥ min_components AND distinct roles ≥ min_roles; OR (3) any single role bucket has ≥ single_role_overflow members. All three are config-tunable; pure topology, no part-number knowledge.

complexity._comment: Unified circuit-complexity score combining component count, net density, cross-block traffic, and label density. Each signal is normalised to [0,1] then weighted; the total is divided by max_score (sum of weights) and compared to split_threshold. Crosses tricky-but-small designs (small RF board with many sub-systems) that bucket rules miss.

local_wire_synthesis._comment: P11 — short-range label-to-wire promotion. After the router emits labels for every signal net, this pass replaces labels with direct Manhattan wires when ALL pins on the net sit within `max_distance_mm` of each other. Long-haul nets (cross-page rails like 3V3 / GND / SDA) keep their labels. Shifts the wire-edges:label-edges ratio toward wires — the visual reason human schematics don't look like floating-label spaghetti.

pin_role_placement._comment: P10 — pin-role aware placement. After the grid-based placer assigns coordinates, this post-pass moves 2-pin satellite passives (decoupling caps, pull-ups, biasing resistors, crystal load caps) to sit adjacent to the specific anchor IC pin they connect to. A decoupling cap that classifier put in MAIN_CONTROLLER role gets moved next to VCC pin, NOT just somewhere inside the MAIN_CONTROLLER grid cell.

community_partition._comment: Connectivity-graph community detection that replaces the role-bucket hierarchy split. Weighted edges (wire=1.0 strong, label=0.6 medium, power=0.2 weak) feed Louvain modularity clustering; clusters are role-named by plurality vote of their members' classifier roles. Used by community_partition.partition_schematic — gated by `enabled` on the consumer side (hierarchical.py).

balance._comment: Post-partition merging: communities below min_members absorb into the largest community; if more than max_sheets remain, smallest ones merge into a final MISC bucket.

anchor_boost._comment: Pre-Louvain weight boost on every edge from an anchor component (MCU / POWER_REGULATOR / SENSOR / WIRELESS / etc.) to its direct neighbours. Pulls the subsystem (anchor + decoupling + crystal + pull-ups) into one community even when the anchor also shares label-edges with other clusters. multiplier=2.5 keeps satellite caps glued to their parent IC.

cross_cluster._comment: When generating sheet pins on the parent, only signal-strength edges become hierarchical labels — power edges merge naturally via power-port symbols and would clutter the parent if exposed.

fallback_zones._comment: When two roles claim the same zone, the second one is bumped to the next unused entry in this order. Spillover roles that exhaust the list re-use the first entry (placer logs a warning).
